en: Elle a examiné comment le débat en philosophie des sciences entre Kuhn et Popper sur les mécanismes du progrès scientifique révèle des tensions fondamentales entre le falsificationnisme et la sociologie de la connaissance scientifique.
hint: She examined how the philosophy of science debate between Kuhn and Popper about the mechanisms of scientific progress reveals fundamental tensions between falsificationism and the sociology of scientific knowledge.
answers: She examined how the philosophy of science debate between Kuhn and Popper about the mechanisms of scientific progress reveals fundamental tensions between falsificationism and the sociology of scientific knowledge.

en: Le concept de dialectique négative, développé par Adorno, propose un mode de pensée critique qui résiste à l'impulsion idéaliste de résoudre les contradictions en fausses synthèses, en préservant le non-identique contre la pensée totalisante.
hint: The concept of negative dialectics, developed by Adorno, proposes a mode of critical thinking that resists the idealist urge to resolve contradictions into false syntheses, preserving the non-identical against totalising thought.
answers: The concept of negative dialectics, developed by Adorno, proposes a mode of critical thinking that resists the idealist urge to resolve contradictions into false syntheses, preserving the non-identical against totalising thought.

en: Il a soutenu que le principe de différence de Rawls, qui permet les inégalités seulement si elles bénéficient au maximum aux moins favorisés, représente une reformulation exigeante de la justice libérale qui va bien au-delà de la simple équité procédurale.
hint: He argued that Rawls's difference principle, which permits inequalities only if they maximally benefit the least advantaged, represents a demanding reformulation of liberal justice that goes far beyond mere procedural fairness.
answers: He argued that Rawls's difference principle, which permits inequalities only if they maximally benefit the least advantaged, represents a demanding reformulation of liberal justice that goes far beyond mere procedural fairness.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept du panoptique, théorisé par Bentham et réinterprété par Foucault, révèle comment l'architecture de surveillance opère comme un mécanisme de pouvoir qui internalise la discipline sans nécessiter d'observation constante.
hint: She maintained that the concept of the panopticon, as theorised by Bentham and reinterpreted by Foucault, reveals how surveillance architecture operates as a mechanism of power that internalises discipline without requiring constant observation.
answers: She maintained that the concept of the panopticon, as theorised by Bentham and reinterpreted by Foucault, reveals how surveillance architecture operates as a mechanism of power that internalises discipline without requiring constant observation.

en: L'antinomie de la raison pure, identifiée par Kant, révèle que la raison humaine, lorsqu'elle est appliquée au-delà de l'expérience possible, génère des arguments contradictoires mais également valides sur la liberté, la causalité, l'infini et l'existence de Dieu.
hint: The antimony of pure reason, as identified by Kant, reveals that human reason when applied beyond possible experience generates contradictory but equally valid arguments about freedom causation infinity and the existence of God.
answers: The antimony of pure reason, as identified by Kant, reveals that human reason when applied beyond possible experience generates contradictory but equally valid arguments about freedom causation infinity and the existence of God.

en: Il a soutenu que l'analyse de l'authenticité chez Heidegger exige d'affronter la possibilité la plus propre de la mort comme condition qui individue le Dasein par rapport au das Man anonyme et révèle l'existence authentique.
hint: He contended that Heidegger's analysis of authenticity requires confronting one's ownmost possibility of death as the condition that individualises Dasein from the anonymous das Man and reveals genuine existence.
answers: He contended that Heidegger's analysis of authenticity requires confronting one's ownmost possibility of death as the condition that individualises Dasein from the anonymous das Man and reveals genuine existence.

en: Elle a examiné comment le concept de différance de Derrida révèle que le sens dans le langage n'est jamais pleinement présent mais est constitué à travers un jeu de différences et de renvois qui rend toute détermination finale du sens impossible.
hint: She examined how Derrida's concept of différance reveals that meaning in language is never fully present but is constituted through a play of differences and deferrals that makes any final determination of meaning impossible.
answers: She examined how Derrida's concept of différance reveals that meaning in language is never fully present but is constituted through a play of differences and deferrals that makes any final determination of meaning impossible.

en: Le concept d'aporie dans le discours philosophique décrit une difficulté logique apparemment irrésoluble ou un puzzle, que Socrate utilisait comme point de départ pour l'enquête philosophique plutôt que comme conclusion.
hint: The concept of aporia in philosophical discourse describes an apparently irresolvable logical difficulty or puzzle, which Socrates used as a starting point for philosophical inquiry rather than a conclusion.
answers: The concept of aporia in philosophical discourse describes an apparently irresolvable logical difficulty or puzzle, which Socrates used as a starting point for philosophical inquiry rather than a conclusion.

en: Il a soutenu que la dialectique hégélienne du maître et de l'esclave révèle un paradoxe fondamental de la domination selon lequel l'identité du maître devient dépendante de la reconnaissance de l'esclave, sapant ainsi la relation même de maîtrise.
hint: He argued that Hegel's dialectic of master and slave reveals a fundamental paradox of domination whereby the master's identity becomes dependent on recognition from the slave thereby undermining the very relation of mastery.
answers: He argued that Hegel's dialectic of master and slave reveals a fundamental paradox of domination whereby the master's identity becomes dependent on recognition from the slave thereby undermining the very relation of mastery.

en: Elle a soutenu que le cadre utilitariste, malgré son attrait intuitif, génère des conclusions troublantes dans les cas où maximiser le bien-être agrégé nécessite de sacrifier les droits et le bien-être des minorités.
hint: She maintained that the utilitarian framework, despite its intuitive appeal, generates troubling conclusions in cases where maximising aggregate welfare requires sacrificing the rights and wellbeing of minorities.
answers: She maintained that the utilitarian framework, despite its intuitive appeal, generates troubling conclusions in cases where maximising aggregate welfare requires sacrificing the rights and wellbeing of minorities.

en: Le problème philosophique de l'identité personnelle demande ce qui fait que vous êtes la même personne dans le temps malgré des changements radicaux dans le corps les croyances et les souvenirs, et si l'identité personnelle est une question de degré ou de nature.
hint: The philosophical problem of personal identity asks what makes you the same person over time across radical changes in body beliefs and memories and whether personal identity is a matter of degree or kind.
answers: The philosophical problem of personal identity asks what makes you the same person over time across radical changes in body beliefs and memories and whether personal identity is a matter of degree or kind.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie des actes de langage, développée par Austin et Searle, démontre que le langage ne décrit pas simplement le monde mais effectue des actions et crée des faits sociaux à travers la force des déclarations institutionnelles.
hint: He contended that the philosophy of language acts, developed by Austin and Searle, demonstrates that language does not merely describe the world but performs actions and creates social facts through the force of institutional declarations.
answers: He contended that the philosophy of language acts, developed by Austin and Searle, demonstrates that language does not merely describe the world but performs actions and creates social facts through the force of institutional declarations.

en: Elle a examiné comment le concept philosophique du sublime, théorisé de Burke à Kant à Lyotard, pointe vers des expériences qui dépassent notre capacité de représentation, révélant les limites de la cognition et de l'esthétique humaines.
hint: She examined how the philosophical concept of the sublime, theorised from Burke to Kant to Lyotard, points to experiences that exceed our capacity for representation revealing the limits of human cognition and aesthetics.
answers: She examined how the philosophical concept of the sublime, theorised from Burke to Kant to Lyotard, points to experiences that exceed our capacity for representation revealing the limits of human cognition and aesthetics.

en: Le débat philosophique sur les fondements des mathématiques entre le platonisme qui soutient que les objets mathématiques existent indépendamment des esprits et le formalisme qui traite les mathématiques comme un jeu formel révèle des questions profondes sur la nature de la vérité mathématique.
hint: The philosophical debate about the foundations of mathematics between Platonism which holds that mathematical objects exist independently of minds and formalism which treats mathematics as a formal game reveals deep questions about the nature of mathematical truth.
answers: The philosophical debate about the foundations of mathematics between Platonism which holds that mathematical objects exist independently of minds and formalism which treats mathematics as a formal game reveals deep questions about the nature of mathematical truth.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de volonté de puissance de Nietzsche ne doit pas être compris comme un désir de domination sur autrui mais comme la pulsion fondamentale vers le dépassement de soi, l'expression créatrice et l'affirmation de la vie.
hint: He argued that Nietzsche's concept of the will to power should not be understood as a desire for domination over others but as the fundamental drive toward self-overcoming creative expression and the affirmation of life.
answers: He argued that Nietzsche's concept of the will to power should not be understood as a desire for domination over others but as the fundamental drive toward self-overcoming creative expression and the affirmation of life.

en: Elle a soutenu que le cogito ergo sum cartésien, bien qu'établissant la certitude de la substance pensante, crée un dualisme problématique corps-esprit que la philosophie a eu du mal à résoudre pendant trois siècles.
hint: She maintained that the Cartesian cogito ergo sum while establishing the certainty of thinking substance creates a problematic mind-body dualism that philosophy has struggled to resolve for three centuries.
answers: She maintained that the Cartesian cogito ergo sum while establishing the certainty of thinking substance creates a problematic mind-body dualism that philosophy has struggled to resolve for three centuries.

en: La critique de l'industrie culturelle par l'École de Francfort soutient que la culture de masse sous le capitalisme ne libère ni ne divertit mais produit des marchandises standardisées qui renforcent le conformisme et la passivité politique.
hint: The Frankfurt School's critique of the culture industry argues that mass culture under capitalism does not liberate or entertain but rather produces standardised commodities that reinforce conformism and political passivity.
answers: The Frankfurt School's critique of the culture industry argues that mass culture under capitalism does not liberate or entertain but rather produces standardised commodities that reinforce conformism and political passivity.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept aristotélicien d'eudaimonia, souvent traduit par bonheur mais signifiant plus précisément épanouissement ou bien-vivre, fournit un compte rendu plus riche de la bonne vie que les conceptions hédoniques modernes.
hint: He contended that Aristotle's concept of eudaimonia which is often translated as happiness but more accurately means flourishing or living well provides a richer account of the good life than modern hedonic conceptions.
answers: He contended that Aristotle's concept of eudaimonia which is often translated as happiness but more accurately means flourishing or living well provides a richer account of the good life than modern hedonic conceptions.

en: Elle a examiné comment le concept du moi nouménal dans la philosophie kantienne, inaccessible à la raison théorique mais présupposé par la raison pratique, fonde l'agentivité morale et la liberté d'une façon que la causalité phénoménale ne peut expliquer.
hint: She examined how the concept of the noumenal self in Kantian philosophy, inaccessible to theoretical reason but presupposed by practical reason, grounds moral agency and freedom in a way that phenomenal causality cannot account for.
answers: She examined how the concept of the noumenal self in Kantian philosophy, inaccessible to theoretical reason but presupposed by practical reason, grounds moral agency and freedom in a way that phenomenal causality cannot account for.

en: Le problème philosophique du libre arbitre face au déterminisme demande si les choix humains sont véritablement libres ou sont ultimement causés par des états antérieurs du monde, générant de profondes tensions entre la responsabilité morale et le naturalisme scientifique.
hint: The philosophical problem of free will versus determinism asks whether human choices are genuinely free or are ultimately caused by prior states of the world generating deep tensions between moral responsibility and scientific naturalism.
answers: The philosophical problem of free will versus determinism asks whether human choices are genuinely free or are ultimately caused by prior states of the world generating deep tensions between moral responsibility and scientific naturalism.

en: Il a soutenu que l'allégorie de la caverne de Platon démontre comment la plupart des êtres humains sont prisonniers des apparences et confondent les images sensorielles avec la vraie réalité, à laquelle seule l'éducation philosophique peut permettre d'accéder.
hint: He argued that Plato's allegory of the cave demonstrates how most human beings are imprisoned by appearances and confuse sensory images with true reality which only philosophical education can enable one to access.
answers: He argued that Plato's allegory of the cave demonstrates how most human beings are imprisoned by appearances and confuse sensory images with true reality which only philosophical education can enable one to access.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de liberté radicale de Sartre, qui affirme que l'existence précède l'essence, implique que les êtres humains sont condamnés à choisir et assument donc une responsabilité totale pour ce qu'ils font d'eux-mêmes.
hint: She maintained that Sartre's concept of radical freedom, which holds that existence precedes essence, implies that human beings are condemned to choose and therefore bear total responsibility for what they make of themselves.
answers: She maintained that Sartre's concept of radical freedom, which holds that existence precedes essence, implies that human beings are condemned to choose and therefore bear total responsibility for what they make of themselves.

en: Le problème du mal pose le défi le plus fondamental au théisme en demandant comment un Dieu omnipotent omniscient et parfaitement bon pourrait permettre l'existence du mal moral et naturel dans le monde.
hint: The problem of evil poses the most fundamental challenge to theism asking how a God who is omnipotent omniscient and perfectly good could permit the existence of moral and natural evil in the world.
answers: The problem of evil poses the most fundamental challenge to theism asking how a God who is omnipotent omniscient and perfectly good could permit the existence of moral and natural evil in the world.

en: Il a soutenu que le problème d'induction de Hume, montrant qu'aucun nombre fini d'observations ne peut justifier logiquement des conclusions universelles, représente un défi permanent aux fondements épistémologiques de la science empirique.
hint: He contended that Hume's problem of induction, showing that no finite number of observations can logically justify universal conclusions, represents a permanent challenge to the epistemological foundations of empirical science.
answers: He contended that Hume's problem of induction, showing that no finite number of observations can logically justify universal conclusions, represents a permanent challenge to the epistemological foundations of empirical science.

en: Elle a examiné comment la philosophie du temps dans les Confessions d'Augustin révèle que le passé n'existe qu'en tant que mémoire, le futur en tant qu'attente et le présent en tant qu'attention, faisant du temps une propriété fondamentale de l'esprit plutôt que du monde.
hint: She examined how the philosophy of time in Augustine's Confessions reveals that the past exists only as memory the future as expectation and the present as attention making time fundamentally a property of the mind rather than the world.
answers: She examined how the philosophy of time in Augustine's Confessions reveals that the past exists only as memory the future as expectation and the present as attention making time fundamentally a property of the mind rather than the world.

en: Le concept d'intersubjectivité en phénoménologie décrit comment notre expérience est fondamentalement façonnée par nos relations avec autrui et comment un monde partagé de sens est constitué à travers ces rencontres.
hint: The concept of intersubjectivity in phenomenology describes how our experience is fundamentally shaped by our relations with others and how a shared world of meaning is constituted through these encounters.
answers: The concept of intersubjectivity in phenomenology describes how our experience is fundamentally shaped by our relations with others and how a shared world of meaning is constituted through these encounters.

en: Il a soutenu que les fondements normatifs des droits de l'homme ne peuvent reposer sur une simple convention juridique mais doivent faire appel à une base morale plus profonde, ancrée dans la dignité, l'agentivité rationnelle ou les besoins humains fondamentaux.
hint: He argued that the normative foundations of human rights cannot rest on mere legal convention but must appeal to a deeper moral basis whether grounded in dignity rational agency or basic human needs.
answers: He argued that the normative foundations of human rights cannot rest on mere legal convention but must appeal to a deeper moral basis whether grounded in dignity rational agency or basic human needs.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de phronèsis ou sagesse pratique dans l'éthique d'Aristote décrit une disposition qui permet de délibérer bien sur ce qui conduit à la bonne vie dans des circonstances particulières plutôt que d'appliquer des règles universelles.
hint: She maintained that the concept of phronesis or practical wisdom in Aristotle's ethics describes a disposition that enables one to deliberate well about what conduces to the good life in particular circumstances rather than applying universal rules.
answers: She maintained that the concept of phronesis or practical wisdom in Aristotle's ethics describes a disposition that enables one to deliberate well about what conduces to the good life in particular circumstances rather than applying universal rules.

en: Le concept philosophique d'émergence décrit comment les systèmes complexes peuvent présenter des propriétés et des comportements qui ne peuvent pas être prédits ou réduits aux propriétés de leurs parties composantes.
hint: The philosophical concept of emergence describes how complex systems can exhibit properties and behaviours that cannot be predicted from or reduced to the properties of their component parts.
answers: The philosophical concept of emergence describes how complex systems can exhibit properties and behaviours that cannot be predicted from or reduced to the properties of their component parts.

en: Il a soutenu que la méthode socratique d'élenchus, en révélant les contradictions au sein des croyances propres de l'interlocuteur, vise non pas à fournir des réponses mais à produire l'aporie qui rend possible la véritable enquête philosophique.
hint: He contended that the Socratic method of elenchus, by revealing the contradictions within the interlocutor's own beliefs, aims not to provide answers but to produce the aporia that makes genuine philosophical inquiry possible.
answers: He contended that the Socratic method of elenchus, by revealing the contradictions within the interlocutor's own beliefs, aims not to provide answers but to produce the aporia that makes genuine philosophical inquiry possible.

en: Elle a examiné comment la philosophie de la religion débat si l'expérience religieuse peut servir de preuve pour l'existence de Dieu ou si ces expériences sont susceptibles d'explications naturalistes alternatives qui sapent leur valeur probatoire.
hint: She examined how the philosophy of religion debates whether religious experience can serve as evidence for the existence of God or whether such experiences are subject to alternative naturalistic explanations that undermine their evidential value.
answers: She examined how the philosophy of religion debates whether religious experience can serve as evidence for the existence of God or whether such experiences are subject to alternative naturalistic explanations that undermine their evidential value.

en: Le concept du cercle herméneutique, central à la théorie de l'interprétation, décrit comment comprendre un texte nécessite de passer entre le tout et ses parties d'une façon qui rend la compréhension à la fois possible et jamais complètement achevée.
hint: The concept of the hermeneutic circle, central to interpretation theory, describes how understanding a text requires moving between the whole and its parts in a way that makes understanding both possible and never fully complete.
answers: The concept of the hermeneutic circle, central to interpretation theory, describes how understanding a text requires moving between the whole and its parts in a way that makes understanding both possible and never fully complete.

en: Il a soutenu que l'expérience de pensée de la machine à expérience proposée par Nozick sape les théories hédonistes du bien-être en montrant que nous valorisons des choses au-delà du plaisir, notamment les accomplissements authentiques et les relations réelles.
hint: He argued that the thought experiment of the experience machine proposed by Nozick undermines hedonistic theories of wellbeing by showing that we value things beyond pleasure namely genuine achievement and real relationships.
answers: He argued that the thought experiment of the experience machine proposed by Nozick undermines hedonistic theories of wellbeing by showing that we value things beyond pleasure namely genuine achievement and real relationships.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de désirs de second ordre, introduit par Harry Frankfurt, révèle que ce qui distingue les personnes n'est pas les désirs de premier ordre mais la capacité de réfléchir et de s'identifier à certains désirs comme véritablement les siens.
hint: She maintained that the concept of second-order desires, introduced by Harry Frankfurt, reveals that what makes persons distinct is not first-order desires but the capacity to reflect on and identify with certain desires as genuinely their own.
answers: She maintained that the concept of second-order desires, introduced by Harry Frankfurt, reveals that what makes persons distinct is not first-order desires but the capacity to reflect on and identify with certain desires as genuinely their own.

en: Le concept philosophique de supervenance décrit une relation de dépendance entre les propriétés de niveau supérieur et inférieur, de telle sorte que tout changement au niveau supérieur nécessite un changement au niveau inférieur, mais pas l'inverse.
hint: The philosophical concept of supervenience describes a relationship of dependence between higher-level and lower-level properties such that any change in the higher-level requires a change in the lower-level but not vice versa.
answers: The philosophical concept of supervenience describes a relationship of dependence between higher-level and lower-level properties such that any change in the higher-level requires a change in the lower-level but not vice versa.

en: Il a soutenu que la distinction philosophique entre le contexte de découverte et le contexte de justification, introduite par Reichenbach, est cruciale pour comprendre la différence entre la façon dont les théories scientifiques sont générées et dont elles sont évaluées.
hint: He contended that the philosophical distinction between the context of discovery and the context of justification, introduced by Reichenbach, is crucial for understanding the difference between how scientific theories are generated and how they are evaluated.
answers: He contended that the philosophical distinction between the context of discovery and the context of justification, introduced by Reichenbach, is crucial for understanding the difference between how scientific theories are generated and how they are evaluated.

en: Elle a examiné comment le libéralisme politique de Rawls tente de développer des principes de justice pouvant être approuvés depuis une variété de doctrines compréhensives, rendant possible la légitimité démocratique dans les sociétés pluralistes.
hint: She examined how Rawls's political liberalism attempts to develop principles of justice that can be endorsed from a variety of comprehensive doctrines making democratic legitimacy possible in pluralist societies.
answers: She examined how Rawls's political liberalism attempts to develop principles of justice that can be endorsed from a variety of comprehensive doctrines making democratic legitimacy possible in pluralist societies.

en: Le concept du problème de Gettier révèle que la définition tripartite traditionnelle de la connaissance comme croyance vraie justifiée est insuffisante car il peut exister des croyances vraies justifiées qui ne constituent pas une connaissance en raison de la chance épistémique.
hint: The concept of the Gettier problem reveals that the traditional tripartite definition of knowledge as justified true belief is insufficient since there can be justified true beliefs that are not knowledge due to epistemic luck.
answers: The concept of the Gettier problem reveals that the traditional tripartite definition of knowledge as justified true belief is insufficient since there can be justified true beliefs that are not knowledge due to epistemic luck.

en: Il a soutenu que le débat philosophique sur le réalisme moral, demandant s'il existe des faits moraux objectifs, a des implications profondes pour la façon dont nous comprenons le désaccord moral, le progrès moral et l'autorité des revendications morales.
hint: He argued that the philosophical debate about moral realism, asking whether there are objective moral facts, has profound implications for how we understand moral disagreement moral progress and the authority of moral claims.
answers: He argued that the philosophical debate about moral realism, asking whether there are objective moral facts, has profound implications for how we understand moral disagreement moral progress and the authority of moral claims.

en: Elle a soutenu que la philosophie de la causalité est confrontée au défi d'expliquer pourquoi la corrélation n'implique pas la causalité et comment nous pouvons distinguer les véritables relations causales des simples régularités dans la nature.
hint: She maintained that the philosophy of causation faces the challenge of explaining why correlation does not imply causation and how we can distinguish genuine causal relations from mere regularities in nature.
answers: She maintained that the philosophy of causation faces the challenge of explaining why correlation does not imply causation and how we can distinguish genuine causal relations from mere regularities in nature.

en: Le concept de concepts éthiques épais, analysé par Bernard Williams, décrit des termes comme cruel ou courageux qui intègrent des dimensions à la fois descriptives et évaluatives, rendant difficile le maintien de la distinction être-devoir.
hint: The concept of thick ethical concepts, as analysed by Bernard Williams, describes terms like cruel or courageous that integrate both descriptive and evaluative dimensions making the is-ought distinction difficult to maintain.
answers: The concept of thick ethical concepts, as analysed by Bernard Williams, describes terms like cruel or courageous that integrate both descriptive and evaluative dimensions making the is-ought distinction difficult to maintain.

en: Il a soutenu que l'argument du langage privé de Wittgenstein démontre qu'un langage purement privé dans lequel les mots renvoient à des expériences sensorielles privées est impossible car le sens requiert des critères publics d'application.
hint: He contended that Wittgenstein's private language argument demonstrates that a purely private language in which words refer to private sensory experiences is impossible since meaning requires public criteria of application.
answers: He contended that Wittgenstein's private language argument demonstrates that a purely private language in which words refer to private sensory experiences is impossible since meaning requires public criteria of application.

en: Elle a examiné comment le débat entre réalistes et antiréalistes en science concerne non seulement l'interprétation de la mécanique quantique mais aussi des questions fondamentales sur si les théories scientifiques décrivent une réalité indépendante ou sont seulement des outils instrumentaux.
hint: She examined how the debate between realists and antirealists in science concerns not just the interpretation of quantum mechanics but fundamental questions about whether scientific theories describe an independent reality or are merely instrumental tools.
answers: She examined how the debate between realists and antirealists in science concerns not just the interpretation of quantum mechanics but fundamental questions about whether scientific theories describe an independent reality or are merely instrumental tools.

en: Le concept philosophique d'acosmisme, associé à certaines lectures de Spinoza, soutient que le monde fini des choses particulières manque de réalité véritable et que seul le tout infini de Dieu-ou-Nature existe vraiment.
hint: The philosophical concept of acosmism, associated with certain readings of Spinoza, holds that the finite world of particular things lacks genuine reality and that only the infinite whole of God-or-Nature truly exists.
answers: The philosophical concept of acosmism, associated with certain readings of Spinoza, holds that the finite world of particular things lacks genuine reality and that only the infinite whole of God-or-Nature truly exists.

en: Il a soutenu que l'analyse philosophique de la justice appliquée aux animaux non humains, aux générations futures et aux personnes ayant des handicaps cognitifs sévères révèle les limites des théories contractariennes qui fondent la justice dans l'accord rationnel.
hint: He argued that the philosophical analysis of justice as it applies to non-human animals future generations and people with severe cognitive disabilities reveals the limits of contractarian theories that ground justice in rational agreement.
answers: He argued that the philosophical analysis of justice as it applies to non-human animals future generations and people with severe cognitive disabilities reveals the limits of contractarian theories that ground justice in rational agreement.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de chance morale, analysé par Nagel et Williams, révèle de profondes tensions dans nos pratiques morales puisque nous louons et blâmons les gens pour des résultats partiellement hors de leur contrôle.
hint: She maintained that the concept of moral luck, as analysed by Nagel and Williams, reveals deep tensions in our moral practices since we praise and blame people for outcomes partly beyond their control.
answers: She maintained that the concept of moral luck, as analysed by Nagel and Williams, reveals deep tensions in our moral practices since we praise and blame people for outcomes partly beyond their control.

en: Le concept d'aliénation chez Hegel et Marx décrit le processus par lequel les êtres humains deviennent étrangers à leur travail, à leurs produits, aux autres êtres humains et finalement à leur propre essence humaine à travers les relations sociales capitalistes.
hint: The concept of alienation in Hegel and Marx describes the process by which human beings become estranged from their labour their products other human beings and ultimately their own human essence through capitalist social relations.
answers: The concept of alienation in Hegel and Marx describes the process by which human beings become estranged from their labour their products other human beings and ultimately their own human essence through capitalist social relations.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de l'Autre, central à l'éthique de Levinas, soutient que le visage de l'Autre fait une demande éthique infinie sur moi qui précède toute ontologie et constitue le fondement de la moralité.
hint: He contended that the concept of the Other, central to Levinas's ethics, holds that the face of the Other makes an infinite ethical demand on me that precedes all ontology and constitutes the foundation of morality.
answers: He contended that the concept of the Other, central to Levinas's ethics, holds that the face of the Other makes an infinite ethical demand on me that precedes all ontology and constitutes the foundation of morality.

en: Elle a examiné comment le débat philosophique sur le constructivisme moral demande si les principes moraux sont découverts comme des faits sur un domaine moral indépendant ou sont construits à travers des procédures de la raison pratique.
hint: She examined how the philosophical debate about moral constructivism asks whether moral principles are discovered as facts about an independent moral realm or are constructed through procedures of practical reason.
answers: She examined how the philosophical debate about moral constructivism asks whether moral principles are discovered as facts about an independent moral realm or are constructed through procedures of practical reason.

en: Le concept de la théologie apophatique ou négative soutient que la nature de Dieu transcende toute description positive et ne peut être abordée qu'en niant les catégories finies, révélant les limites du langage humain sur le divin.
hint: The concept of the apophatic or negative theology holds that God's nature transcends all positive description and can only be approached by negating finite categories revealing the limits of human language about the divine.
answers: The concept of the apophatic or negative theology holds that God's nature transcends all positive description and can only be approached by negating finite categories revealing the limits of human language about the divine.

en: Il a soutenu que l'analyse philosophique du récit révèle comment les êtres humains comprennent leur vie à travers des structures temporelles de mise en intrigue qui imposent du sens à la contingence de l'expérience vécue.
hint: He argued that the philosophical analysis of narrative reveals how human beings understand their lives through temporal structures of emplotment that impose meaning on the contingency of lived experience.
answers: He argued that the philosophical analysis of narrative reveals how human beings understand their lives through temporal structures of emplotment that impose meaning on the contingency of lived experience.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'éthique du soin, développé par Carol Gilligan et Nel Noddings en opposition à l'éthique de justice abstraite de Kohlberg, met l'accent sur la signification morale des relations particulières et la réactivité contextuelle.
hint: She maintained that the concept of care ethics, developed by Carol Gilligan and Nel Noddings in opposition to Kohlberg's abstract justice ethics, emphasises the moral significance of particular relationships and contextual responsiveness.
answers: She maintained that the concept of care ethics, developed by Carol Gilligan and Nel Noddings in opposition to Kohlberg's abstract justice ethics, emphasises the moral significance of particular relationships and contextual responsiveness.

en: Le problème philosophique du critère demande comment nous pouvons savoir quelles croyances constituent une connaissance sans avoir déjà un critère de connaissance, créant une circularité épistémologique fondamentale.
hint: The philosophical problem of the criterion asks how we can know which of our beliefs constitute knowledge without already having a criterion of knowledge creating a fundamental epistemological circularity.
answers: The philosophical problem of the criterion asks how we can know which of our beliefs constitute knowledge without already having a criterion of knowledge creating a fundamental epistemological circularity.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept philosophique d'altérité, central à l'éthique post-structuraliste, insiste sur le fait que le véritable respect pour l'Autre exige de résister à la tentation de réduire la différence à la mêmeté à travers des cadres totalisants.
hint: He contended that the philosophical concept of alterity, central to post-structuralist ethics, insists that genuine respect for the Other demands we resist the temptation to reduce difference to sameness through totalising frameworks.
answers: He contended that the philosophical concept of alterity, central to post-structuralist ethics, insists that genuine respect for the Other demands we resist the temptation to reduce difference to sameness through totalising frameworks.

en: Elle a examiné comment le débat épistémologique entre l'externalisme et l'internalisme en philosophie de l'esprit concerne si ce qui justifie les croyances dépend uniquement de facteurs internes à l'esprit ou aussi de relations causales externes au monde.
hint: She examined how the epistemological debate between externalism and internalism in philosophy of mind concerns whether what justifies beliefs depends solely on factors internal to the mind or also on external causal relations to the world.
answers: She examined how the epistemological debate between externalism and internalism in philosophy of mind concerns whether what justifies beliefs depends solely on factors internal to the mind or also on external causal relations to the world.

en: Le concept de double conscience, développé par W.E.B. Du Bois, décrit l'expérience psychologique des Afro-Américains qui doivent se voir à travers leurs propres yeux et à travers les yeux d'une société racialement dominante qui les déshumanise.
hint: The concept of double consciousness, developed by W.E.B. Du Bois, describes the psychological experience of African Americans who must see themselves through their own eyes and through the eyes of a racially dominant society that dehumanises them.
answers: The concept of double consciousness, developed by W.E.B. Du Bois, describes the psychological experience of African Americans who must see themselves through their own eyes and through the eyes of a racially dominant society that dehumanises them.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de ressentiment, analysé par Nietzsche, décrit la psychologie réactive de ceux qui n't ont pas le pouvoir d'affirmer des valeurs directement et créent plutôt des valeurs négatives en condamnant ce qu'ils ne peuvent pas atteindre.
hint: He argued that the concept of ressentiment, as analysed by Nietzsche, describes the reactive psychology of those who lack the power to affirm values directly and instead create negative values by condemning what they cannot attain.
answers: He argued that the concept of ressentiment, as analysed by Nietzsche, describes the reactive psychology of those who lack the power to affirm values directly and instead create negative values by condemning what they cannot attain.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept philosophique d'incarnation, central chez des phénoménologues comme Merleau-Ponty, remet en cause le dualisme cartésien corps-esprit en montrant que la conscience est toujours déjà incarnée et que le corps est le site primaire de notre être-au-monde.
hint: She maintained that the philosophical concept of embodiment, central to phenomenologists like Merleau-Ponty, challenges the Cartesian mind-body dualism by showing that consciousness is always already embodied and that the body is the primary site of our being-in-the-world.
answers: She maintained that the philosophical concept of embodiment, central to phenomenologists like Merleau-Ponty, challenges the Cartesian mind-body dualism by showing that consciousness is always already embodied and that the body is the primary site of our being-in-the-world.

en: Le concept de l'éternel retour dans la philosophie de Nietzsche sert d'hypothèse cosmologique, de test psychologique de l'affirmation et d'impératif éthique exigeant que nous vivions de telle sorte que nous voudrions que chaque moment se répète à l'infini.
hint: The concept of the eternal return in Nietzsche's philosophy serves as a cosmological hypothesis a psychological test of affirmation and an ethical imperative demanding that we live such that we would will each moment to recur infinitely.
answers: The concept of the eternal return in Nietzsche's philosophy serves as a cosmological hypothesis a psychological test of affirmation and an ethical imperative demanding that we live such that we would will each moment to recur infinitely.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept marxien de fétichisme de la marchandise décrit comment les relations sociales entre les personnes se dissimulent derrière les relations apparentes entre les choses, rendant le caractère social de la production invisible.
hint: He contended that the Marxian concept of commodity fetishism describes how the social relations between people become concealed behind the apparent relations between things making the social character of production invisible.
answers: He contended that the Marxian concept of commodity fetishism describes how the social relations between people become concealed behind the apparent relations between things making the social character of production invisible.

en: Elle a examiné comment le débat philosophique sur la responsabilité personnelle à la lumière du déterminisme neurologique remet en cause nos pratiques morales ordinaires de louange, de blâme, de punition et de récompense.
hint: She examined how the philosophical debate about personal responsibility in light of neurological determinism challenges our ordinary moral practices of praise blame punishment and reward.
answers: She examined how the philosophical debate about personal responsibility in light of neurological determinism challenges our ordinary moral practices of praise blame punishment and reward.

en: Le concept du paradoxe de l'hédonisme révèle que la poursuite directe du plaisir tend à se miner elle-même puisque le plaisir vient comme un sous-produit d'autres activités poursuivies pour elles-mêmes plutôt que comme un but en soi.
hint: The concept of the paradox of hedonism reveals that the direct pursuit of pleasure tends to undermine itself since pleasure comes as a byproduct of other activities pursued for their own sake rather than as a goal in itself.
answers: The concept of the paradox of hedonism reveals that the direct pursuit of pleasure tends to undermine itself since pleasure comes as a byproduct of other activities pursued for their own sake rather than as a goal in itself.

en: Il a soutenu que le débat en philosophie de l'esprit entre le fonctionnalisme qui définit les états mentaux par leurs rôles causaux et les théories de la conscience phénoménale révèle un fossé fondamental entre les descriptions fonctionnelles et le caractère qualitatif de l'expérience.
hint: He argued that the debate in philosophy of mind between functionalism, which defines mental states by their causal roles, and phenomenal consciousness theories reveals a fundamental gap between functional descriptions and the qualitative character of experience.
answers: He argued that the debate in philosophy of mind between functionalism, which defines mental states by their causal roles, and phenomenal consciousness theories reveals a fundamental gap between functional descriptions and the qualitative character of experience.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept du voile de maya dans la philosophie de Schopenhauer décrit comment le principium individuationis dissimule l'unité sous-jacente de la volonté et crée l'illusion d'un monde de choses distinctes et séparées.
hint: She maintained that the concept of the veil of maya in Schopenhauer's philosophy describes how the principium individuationis conceals the underlying unity of the will and creates the illusion of a world of distinct separate things.
answers: She maintained that the concept of the veil of maya in Schopenhauer's philosophy describes how the principium individuationis conceals the underlying unity of the will and creates the illusion of a world of distinct separate things.

en: Le problème philosophique de l'unité de la conscience demande comment les nombreux contenus différents de l'expérience consciente sont liés en une seule expérience unifiée et si les neurosciences peuvent fournir une explication adéquate.
hint: The philosophical problem of the unity of consciousness asks how the many different contents of conscious experience are bound together into a single unified experience and whether neuroscience can provide an adequate explanation.
answers: The philosophical problem of the unity of consciousness asks how the many different contents of conscious experience are bound together into a single unified experience and whether neuroscience can provide an adequate explanation.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept philosophique du monde vécu, développé par Husserl et Schutz, décrit l'arrière-plan pré-donné de pratiques, de significations et d'hypothèses considérées comme allant de soi, qui forme l'horizon non-thématique de toute expérience.
hint: He contended that the philosophical concept of the lifeworld, as developed by Husserl and Schutz, describes the pre-given background of taken-for-granted practices meanings and assumptions that forms the unthematic horizon of all experience.
answers: He contended that the philosophical concept of the lifeworld, as developed by Husserl and Schutz, describes the pre-given background of taken-for-granted practices meanings and assumptions that forms the unthematic horizon of all experience.

en: Elle a examiné comment le concept de reconnaissance, central à la philosophie sociale et politique contemporaine, révèle que les luttes pour la justice ne sont pas simplement une question de redistribution des ressources mais d'être vu et reconnu comme personne à part entière.
hint: She examined how the concept of recognition, central to contemporary social and political philosophy, reveals that struggles for justice are not simply about redistribution of resources but about being seen and acknowledged as a full person.
answers: She examined how the concept of recognition, central to contemporary social and political philosophy, reveals that struggles for justice are not simply about redistribution of resources but about being seen and acknowledged as a full person.

en: Le paradoxe de la tolérance dans les démocraties libérales contemporaines se manifeste dans la question de savoir si les plateformes, les entreprises médiatiques et les États doivent activement supprimer le discours intolérant ou le permettre au nom de la liberté d'expression, créant de véritables dilemmes.
hint: The paradox of tolerance in contemporary liberal democracies manifests in whether platforms media companies and states should actively suppress intolerant speech or allow it in the name of free expression creating genuine dilemmas.
answers: The paradox of tolerance in contemporary liberal democracies manifests in whether platforms media companies and states should actively suppress intolerant speech or allow it in the name of free expression creating genuine dilemmas.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'injustice épistémique, introduit par Miranda Fricker, identifie une forme de tort qui est spécifiquement épistémique ciblant les personnes dans leur capacité de détenteurs de savoir soit par l'injustice testimoniale soit par l'injustice herméneutique.
hint: He argued that the concept of epistemic injustice, introduced by Miranda Fricker, identifies a form of wrongdoing that is specifically epistemic targeting people in their capacity as knowers either through testimonial injustice or hermeneutical injustice.
answers: He argued that the concept of epistemic injustice, introduced by Miranda Fricker, identifies a form of wrongdoing that is specifically epistemic targeting people in their capacity as knowers either through testimonial injustice or hermeneutical injustice.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de mondéité, analysé par Heidegger, révèle que les choses n'apparaissent pas d'abord comme de simples objets mais sont toujours déjà rencontrées dans un réseau d'implications pratiques qui leur donne leur signification.
hint: She maintained that the concept of worldhood, as analysed by Heidegger, reveals that things do not first appear as bare objects but are always already encountered within a network of practical involvements that gives them their meaning.
answers: She maintained that the concept of worldhood, as analysed by Heidegger, reveals that things do not first appear as bare objects but are always already encountered within a network of practical involvements that gives them their meaning.

en: Le concept de tragédie en philosophie politique, analysé par Bernard Williams, décrit des situations où les conflits moraux sont véritablement irréductibles et où bien agir laisse encore des résidus de méfaits qui devraient engendrer un regret de l'agent.
hint: The concept of tragedy in political philosophy, as analysed by Bernard Williams, describes situations where moral conflicts are genuinely irresolvable and where acting well still leaves residue of wrongdoing that should generate agent regret.
answers: The concept of tragedy in political philosophy, as analysed by Bernard Williams, describes situations where moral conflicts are genuinely irresolvable and where acting well still leaves residue of wrongdoing that should generate agent regret.

en: Il a soutenu que l'analyse philosophique de la mémoire révèle que ce que nous nous rappelons n'est pas une copie fidèle du passé mais un acte constructif façonné par les préoccupations présentes les croyances antérieures et les cadres sociaux de remémoration.
hint: He contended that the philosophical analysis of memory reveals that what we remember is not a faithful copy of the past but a constructive act shaped by present concerns prior beliefs and social frameworks of remembrance.
answers: He contended that the philosophical analysis of memory reveals that what we remember is not a faithful copy of the past but a constructive act shaped by present concerns prior beliefs and social frameworks of remembrance.

en: Elle a examiné comment l'argument cosmologique pour l'existence de Dieu tente de raisonner à partir de faits contingents sur le monde vers un être nécessaire qui explique l'existence du monde mais fait face à l'objection de la cause non causée.
hint: She examined how the concept of cosmological argument for God's existence attempts to reason from contingent facts about the world to a necessary being that explains the world's existence but faces the objection of the uncaused cause.
answers: She examined how the concept of cosmological argument for God's existence attempts to reason from contingent facts about the world to a necessary being that explains the world's existence but faces the objection of the uncaused cause.

en: Le concept philosophique de l'inquiétante étrangeté, chez Freud et Heidegger, décrit une expérience d'estrangement dans laquelle ce qui est familier apparaît soudainement comme étranger, révélant la fragilité de notre sentiment habituel d'être chez soi dans le monde.
hint: The philosophical concept of the uncanny, in Freud and Heidegger, describes an experience of estrangement in which what is familiar suddenly appears alien revealing the fragility of our habitual sense of being at home in the world.
answers: The philosophical concept of the uncanny, in Freud and Heidegger, describes an experience of estrangement in which what is familiar suddenly appears alien revealing the fragility of our habitual sense of being at home in the world.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept philosophique de l'Autre, central à l'ontologie phénoménologique de Sartre, révèle que le regard de l'Autre me transforme en objet, sapant mon projet d'être libre et générant un conflit fondamental au cœur des relations humaines.
hint: He argued that the philosophical concept of the Other, as central to Sartre's phenomenological ontology, reveals that the Other's look transforms me into an object undermining my project of being free and generating fundamental conflict at the heart of human relations.
answers: He argued that the philosophical concept of the Other, as central to Sartre's phenomenological ontology, reveals that the Other's look transforms me into an object undermining my project of being free and generating fundamental conflict at the heart of human relations.

en: Elle a soutenu que la méthode transcendantale dans la philosophie critique de Kant procède en demandant quelles conditions doivent être présupposées comme nécessaires pour la possibilité de l'expérience, de la connaissance et de la moralité, fournissant des fondements a priori.
hint: She maintained that the transcendental method in Kant's critical philosophy proceeds by asking what conditions must be presupposed as necessary for the possibility of experience knowledge and morality providing a priori foundations.
answers: She maintained that the transcendental method in Kant's critical philosophy proceeds by asking what conditions must be presupposed as necessary for the possibility of experience knowledge and morality providing a priori foundations.

en: Le débat philosophique entre le réalisme moral et l'anti-réalisme moral porte sur la question de savoir si les affirmations morales peuvent être vraies ou fausses en un sens objectif ou si elles expriment simplement des attitudes des préférences ou des normes socialement construites sans vérité indépendante de l'esprit.
hint: The philosophical debate between moral realism and moral anti-realism concerns whether moral claims can be true or false in an objective sense or whether they merely express attitudes preferences or socially constructed norms with no mind-independent truth.
answers: The philosophical debate between moral realism and moral anti-realism concerns whether moral claims can be true or false in an objective sense or whether they merely express attitudes preferences or socially constructed norms with no mind-independent truth.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'expressivisme en métaéthique, développé par Ayer puis Blackburn et Gibbard, soutient que les énoncés moraux ne sont pas des descriptions de faits mais des expressions d'attitudes pour ou contre, avec le quasi-réalisme tentant de gagner le droit au discours moral.
hint: He argued that the concept of expressivism in metaethics, developed by Ayer and later Blackburn and Gibbard, holds that moral utterances are not descriptions of facts but expressions of pro or con attitudes with quasi-realism attempting to earn the right to moral discourse.
answers: He argued that the concept of expressivism in metaethics, developed by Ayer and later Blackburn and Gibbard, holds that moral utterances are not descriptions of facts but expressions of pro or con attitudes with quasi-realism attempting to earn the right to moral discourse.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de théorie de l'erreur en métaéthique, associé à J.L. Mackie, soutient que les affirmations morales visent à décrire des faits moraux objectifs mais puisque de tels faits n'existent pas toutes les affirmations morales positives sont systématiquement fausses.
hint: She maintained that the concept of error theory in metaethics, associated with J.L. Mackie, holds that moral claims aim to describe objective moral facts but since no such facts exist all positive moral claims are systematically false.
answers: She maintained that the concept of error theory in metaethics, associated with J.L. Mackie, holds that moral claims aim to describe objective moral facts but since no such facts exist all positive moral claims are systematically false.

en: Le concept d'intentionnalité dans la phénoménologie de Husserl, qu'il a hérité de Brentano, soutient que la conscience est toujours conscience de quelque chose, signifiant que tout acte mental est dirigé vers un objet intentionnel dans un mode spécifique.
hint: The concept of intentionality in Husserl's phenomenology, which he inherited from Brentano, holds that consciousness is always consciousness of something meaning every mental act is directed toward an intentional object in a specific mode.
answers: The concept of intentionality in Husserl's phenomenology, which he inherited from Brentano, holds that consciousness is always consciousness of something meaning every mental act is directed toward an intentional object in a specific mode.

en: Il a soutenu que la distinction de Heidegger entre l'outil à-portée-de-la-main et l'outil sous-la-main révèle que le mode d'être le plus primordial des choses est leur disponibilité pratique pour l'usage et non leur présence théorique comme objets de contemplation.
hint: He contended that Heidegger's distinction between ready-to-hand and present-at-hand equipment reveals that the most primordial mode of being of things is their practical readiness for use not their theoretical presence as objects of contemplation.
answers: He contended that Heidegger's distinction between ready-to-hand and present-at-hand equipment reveals that the most primordial mode of being of things is their practical readiness for use not their theoretical presence as objects of contemplation.

en: Elle a soutenu que le monisme de substance de Spinoza affirme qu'il n'existe qu'une seule substance infinie qu'il identifie à Dieu ou à la Nature et que ce que nous appelons esprits et corps ne sont que des attributs de cette unique substance pensée sous différents attributs.
hint: She argued that Spinoza's substance monism holds that there is only one infinite substance which he identifies with God or Nature and that what we call minds and bodies are merely attributes of this single substance thought of under different attributes.
answers: She argued that Spinoza's substance monism holds that there is only one infinite substance which he identifies with God or Nature and that what we call minds and bodies are merely attributes of this single substance thought of under different attributes.

en: Le concept philosophique des mondes possibles, développé par Leibniz et repris par Kripke et Lewis, nous permet d'analyser les affirmations modales sur ce qui est nécessaire ou possible en termes de ce qui est vrai dans tous ou certains mondes possibles.
hint: The philosophical concept of possible worlds, developed by Leibniz and revived by Kripke and Lewis, allows us to analyse modal claims about what is necessary or possible in terms of what is true across all or some possible worlds.
answers: The philosophical concept of possible worlds, developed by Leibniz and revived by Kripke and Lewis, allows us to analyse modal claims about what is necessary or possible in terms of what is true across all or some possible worlds.

en: Il a soutenu que la monadologie de Leibniz soutient que la réalité est composée d'un nombre infini de substances spirituelles simples non étendues appelées monades, chacune reflétant l'univers entier depuis sa propre perspective sans interaction réelle entre elles.
hint: He maintained that Leibniz's monadology holds that reality is composed of an infinite number of simple non-extended spiritual substances called monads each of which mirrors the entire universe from its own perspective with no real interaction between them.
answers: He maintained that Leibniz's monadology holds that reality is composed of an infinite number of simple non-extended spiritual substances called monads each of which mirrors the entire universe from its own perspective with no real interaction between them.

en: Elle a soutenu que la distinction philosophique entre jugements analytiques et synthétiques, introduite par Kant, sépare les jugements dont les prédicats sont contenus dans le sujet de ceux qui ajoutent de nouvelles informations, les jugements synthétiques a priori étant les plus philosophiquement significatifs.
hint: She contended that the philosophical distinction between analytic and synthetic judgments, introduced by Kant, separates judgments whose predicates are contained in the subject from judgments that add new information with synthetic a priori judgments being most philosophically significant.
answers: She contended that the philosophical distinction between analytic and synthetic judgments, introduced by Kant, separates judgments whose predicates are contained in the subject from judgments that add new information with synthetic a priori judgments being most philosophically significant.

en: La division analytique versus continentale en philosophie reflète des engagements méthodologiques profondément différents, la philosophie analytique privilégiant la clarté, la rigueur logique et l'argumentation fragmentée tandis que la philosophie continentale favorise l'ancrage historique, la grande synthèse et l'engagement existentiel.
hint: The analytic versus continental divide in philosophy reflects deeply different methodological commitments analytic philosophy prizing clarity logical rigor and piecemeal argument while continental philosophy favours historical situatedness grand synthesis and existential engagement.
answers: The analytic versus continental divide in philosophy reflects deeply different methodological commitments analytic philosophy prizing clarity logical rigor and piecemeal argument while continental philosophy favours historical situatedness grand synthesis and existential engagement.

en: Il a examiné comment l'argument ontologique pour l'existence de Dieu, formulé par Anselme puis Descartes et Leibniz, tente de déduire l'existence de Dieu du concept même d'un être dont on ne peut concevoir de plus grand, mais fait face à l'objection que l'existence n'est pas un prédicat.
hint: He examined how the ontological argument for God's existence, formulated by Anselm and later Descartes and Leibniz, attempts to derive God's existence from the very concept of a being than which none greater can be conceived but faces the objection that existence is not a predicate.
answers: He examined how the ontological argument for God's existence, formulated by Anselm and later Descartes and Leibniz, attempts to derive God's existence from the very concept of a being than which none greater can be conceived but faces the objection that existence is not a predicate.

en: L'argument téléologique pour l'existence de Dieu, connu aussi comme l'argument du dessein, raisonne à partir de l'ordre apparent et du but dans le monde naturel vers un concepteur intelligent, mais Hume et Darwin ont fourni des critiques dévastatrices de cette inférence.
hint: The teleological argument for God's existence, also known as the argument from design, reasons from apparent order and purpose in the natural world to an intelligent designer but Hume and Darwin provided devastating critiques of this inference.
answers: The teleological argument for God's existence, also known as the argument from design, reasons from apparent order and purpose in the natural world to an intelligent designer but Hume and Darwin provided devastating critiques of this inference.

en: Elle a soutenu que la théorie de la vérité par correspondance, longtemps dominante en philosophie, soutient qu'une proposition est vraie si et seulement si elle correspond à un fait dans le monde, mais fait face à de sérieuses difficultés pour spécifier ce que sont les faits et en quoi consiste la correspondance.
hint: She argued that the correspondence theory of truth, long dominant in philosophy, holds that a proposition is true if and only if it corresponds to a fact in the world but faces serious difficulties in specifying what facts are and what correspondence consists in.
answers: She argued that the correspondence theory of truth, long dominant in philosophy, holds that a proposition is true if and only if it corresponds to a fact in the world but faces serious difficulties in specifying what facts are and what correspondence consists in.

en: Il a soutenu que la théorie pragmatiste de la vérité, avancée par Peirce, James et Dewey, soutient que la vérité ne concerne pas la correspondance avec une réalité indépendante de l'esprit mais ce qui fonctionne, ce qui est utile pour guider l'action et satisfaire les buts humains.
hint: He contended that the pragmatist theory of truth, advanced by Pierce James and Dewey, holds that truth is not about correspondence to mind-independent reality but about what works what is useful for guiding action and satisfying human purposes.
answers: He contended that the pragmatist theory of truth, advanced by Pierce James and Dewey, holds that truth is not about correspondence to mind-independent reality but about what works what is useful for guiding action and satisfying human purposes.

en: Les théories déflationnistes de la vérité soutiennent que la vérité n'est pas une propriété substantielle méritant une analyse philosophique profonde mais simplement un dispositif logique pour endorser des assertions ou généraliser sur des propositions avec Ramsey, Ayer et Horwich comme partisans clés.
hint: The deflationary theories of truth hold that truth is not a substantial property worthy of deep philosophical analysis but merely a logical device for endorsing assertions or generalising over propositions with Ramsey Ayer and Horwich as key proponents.
answers: The deflationary theories of truth hold that truth is not a substantial property worthy of deep philosophical analysis but merely a logical device for endorsing assertions or generalising over propositions with Ramsey Ayer and Horwich as key proponents.

en: Elle a examiné comment la philosophie des mathématiques fait face à la tension fondationnelle entre le platonisme qui soutient que les objets mathématiques existent indépendamment des esprits et le nominalisme qui nie l'existence indépendante des entités mathématiques abstraites.
hint: She examined how the philosophy of mathematics faces the foundational tension between Platonism which holds that mathematical objects exist independently of minds and nominalism which denies the independent existence of abstract mathematical entities.
answers: She examined how the philosophy of mathematics faces the foundational tension between Platonism which holds that mathematical objects exist independently of minds and nominalism which denies the independent existence of abstract mathematical entities.

en: Il a soutenu que l'intuitionnisme mathématique, développé par Brouwer, soutient que la vérité mathématique n'est pas découverte mais construite par l'esprit mathématique, rejetant le principe du tiers exclu pour les domaines infinis comme dénué de sens sans preuve constructive.
hint: He argued that mathematical intuitionism, developed by Brouwer, holds that mathematical truth is not discovered but constructed by the mathematical mind rejecting the law of excluded middle for infinite domains as meaningless without a constructive proof.
answers: He argued that mathematical intuitionism, developed by Brouwer, holds that mathematical truth is not discovered but constructed by the mathematical mind rejecting the law of excluded middle for infinite domains as meaningless without a constructive proof.

en: Le concept d'épistémologie sociale, développé par des philosophes tels qu'Alvin Goldman et Miriam Solomon, examine comment les structures, les processus et les institutions sociales affectent la production, la distribution et l'évaluation du savoir.
hint: The concept of social epistemology, developed by philosophers such as Alvin Goldman and Miriam Solomon, examines how social structures processes and institutions affect the production distribution and evaluation of knowledge.
answers: The concept of social epistemology, developed by philosophers such as Alvin Goldman and Miriam Solomon, examines how social structures processes and institutions affect the production distribution and evaluation of knowledge.

en: Elle a soutenu que la philosophie confucéenne, enracinée dans les enseignements de Confucius et élaborée par Mencius et Xunzi, est centrée sur l'éthique relationnelle et la cultivation de la vertu à travers des relations appropriées, des rôles sociaux et la pratique rituelle.
hint: She maintained that Confucian philosophy, rooted in the teachings of Confucius and elaborated by Mencius and Xunzi, centres on relational ethics and the cultivation of virtue through proper relationships social roles and ritual practice.
answers: She maintained that Confucian philosophy, rooted in the teachings of Confucius and elaborated by Mencius and Xunzi, centres on relational ethics and the cultivation of virtue through proper relationships social roles and ritual practice.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie bouddhiste, dans ses nombreuses écoles, est unifiée par l'analyse de la souffrance, de l'impermanence et du non-soi, et propose la libération par la pratique de la Noble Voie Octuple, de la pleine conscience et de l'insight dans l'origination dépendante.
hint: He contended that Buddhist philosophy, across its many schools, is unified by the analysis of suffering impermanence and non-self and proposes liberation through the Noble Eightfold Path practice of mindfulness and insight into dependent origination.
answers: He contended that Buddhist philosophy, across its many schools, is unified by the analysis of suffering impermanence and non-self and proposes liberation through the Noble Eightfold Path practice of mindfulness and insight into dependent origination.

en: Le concept de philosophie ubuntu dans les traditions philosophiques africaines exprime que la personnéité est fondamentalement communautaire plutôt qu'individuelle, capturé dans l'aphorisme nguni umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu signifiant qu'une personne est une personne grâce aux autres personnes.
hint: The concept of ubuntu philosophy in African philosophical traditions expresses that personhood is fundamentally communal rather than individual captured in the Nguni aphorism umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu meaning a person is a person through other persons.
answers: The concept of ubuntu philosophy in African philosophical traditions expresses that personhood is fundamentally communal rather than individual captured in the Nguni aphorism umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu meaning a person is a person through other persons.

en: Elle a soutenu que l'éthique environnementale défie le cadre anthropocentrique dominant dans la philosophie occidentale en défendant la valeur intrinsèque de la nature, des communautés écologiques et des animaux non humains au-delà de leur valeur instrumentale pour les buts humains.
hint: She argued that environmental ethics challenges the dominant anthropocentric framework in Western philosophy by arguing for the intrinsic value of nature ecological communities and non-human animals beyond their instrumental value for human purposes.
answers: She argued that environmental ethics challenges the dominant anthropocentric framework in Western philosophy by arguing for the intrinsic value of nature ecological communities and non-human animals beyond their instrumental value for human purposes.

en: Il a soutenu que le débat entre l'éthique globale utilitariste de Peter Singer et la morale de sens commun révèle que l'impartialisme strict peut exiger une redistribution radicale des richesses d'une façon qui entre en conflit avec nos intuitions morales ordinaires sur les obligations spéciales.
hint: He maintained that the debate between Peter Singer's utilitarian global ethics and commonsense morality reveals that strict impartialism may demand radical redistribution of wealth in ways that conflict with our ordinary moral intuitions about special obligations.
answers: He maintained that the debate between Peter Singer's utilitarian global ethics and commonsense morality reveals that strict impartialism may demand radical redistribution of wealth in ways that conflict with our ordinary moral intuitions about special obligations.

en: La philosophie politique de la reconnaissance, développée par Axel Honneth en s'appuyant sur Hegel, soutient que les pathologies de la vie sociale moderne peuvent être comprises comme des échecs de reconnaissance et que le progrès social requiert l'expansion des sphères de reconnaissance mutuelle.
hint: The political philosophy of recognition, developed by Axel Honneth building on Hegel, argues that the pathologies of modern social life can be understood as failures of recognition and that social progress requires expanding spheres of mutual recognition.
answers: The political philosophy of recognition, developed by Axel Honneth building on Hegel, argues that the pathologies of modern social life can be understood as failures of recognition and that social progress requires expanding spheres of mutual recognition.

en: Elle a soutenu que le cadre de justice de Nancy Fraser distingue entre redistribution, reconnaissance et représentation comme trois dimensions analytiquement distinctes de la justice sociale qui doivent toutes être abordées pour une véritable transformation sociale.
hint: She contended that Nancy Fraser's framework for justice distinguishes between redistribution recognition and representation as three analytically distinct dimensions of social justice that must all be addressed for genuine social transformation.
answers: She contended that Nancy Fraser's framework for justice distinguishes between redistribution recognition and representation as three analytically distinct dimensions of social justice that must all be addressed for genuine social transformation.

en: Il a soutenu que le cadre de devoir négatif de Thomas Pogge pour la justice globale affirme que les pays riches ne se contentent pas de ne pas aider les pauvres du monde mais leur nuisent activement à travers des institutions internationales injustes nécessitant une action corrective.
hint: He argued that Thomas Pogge's negative duty framework for global justice holds that affluent countries are not merely failing to help the global poor but are actively harming them through unjust international institutions requiring remedial action.
answers: He argued that Thomas Pogge's negative duty framework for global justice holds that affluent countries are not merely failing to help the global poor but are actively harming them through unjust international institutions requiring remedial action.

en: La théorie de la démocratie délibérative de Jürgen Habermas soutient que la légitimité politique découle de la délibération publique dans des conditions de discours rationnel où seule la force du meilleur argument devrait déterminer les résultats.
hint: The deliberative democratic theory of Jurgen Habermas holds that political legitimacy derives from public deliberation under conditions of rational discourse where only the force of the better argument ought to determine outcomes.
answers: The deliberative democratic theory of Jurgen Habermas holds that political legitimacy derives from public deliberation under conditions of rational discourse where only the force of the better argument ought to determine outcomes.

en: Elle a soutenu que la théorie démocratique agonistique de Chantal Mouffe, par contraste avec le modèle délibératif de Habermas, insiste que l'antagonisme est irréductible en politique et que la démocratie devrait transformer les ennemis en adversaires qui contestent au sein d'institutions partagées.
hint: She maintained that Chantal Mouffe's agonistic democratic theory, in contrast to Habermas's deliberative model, insists that antagonism is irreducible in politics and that democracy should transform enemies into adversaries who contest within shared institutions.
answers: She maintained that Chantal Mouffe's agonistic democratic theory, in contrast to Habermas's deliberative model, insists that antagonism is irreducible in politics and that democracy should transform enemies into adversaries who contest within shared institutions.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie politique de Hannah Arendt distingue le travail l'œuvre et l'action comme modes distincts de l'activité humaine, l'action dans le domaine public étant la forme la plus haute de liberté humaine et le domaine propre de la politique.
hint: He contended that Hannah Arendt's political philosophy distinguishes between labour work and action as distinct modes of human activity with action in the public realm being the highest form of human freedom and the proper domain of politics.
answers: He contended that Hannah Arendt's political philosophy distinguishes between labour work and action as distinct modes of human activity with action in the public realm being the highest form of human freedom and the proper domain of politics.

en: La théorie critique de Walter Benjamin, particulièrement son concept d'image dialectique et sa critique de l'historicisme, soutient que le passé doit être saisi dans des moments de danger pour être racheté pour la génération présente à travers la mémoire révolutionnaire.
hint: The critical theory of Walter Benjamin, particularly his concept of the dialectical image and his critique of historicism, argues that the past must be seized in moments of danger to be redeemed for the present generation through revolutionary memory.
answers: The critical theory of Walter Benjamin, particularly his concept of the dialectical image and his critique of historicism, argues that the past must be seized in moments of danger to be redeemed for the present generation through revolutionary memory.

en: Elle a soutenu que la théorie critique de Herbert Marcuse, particulièrement dans L'Homme unidimensionnel, analyse comment les sociétés industrielles avancées éliminent la pensée oppositionnelle en absorbant la critique dans la culture commodifiée et en générant une fausse conscience de contentement.
