hint: She argued that Herbert Marcuse's critical theory, particularly in One Dimensional Man, analyses how advanced industrial societies eliminate oppositional thought by absorbing critique into commodified culture and generating a false consciousness of contentment.
answers: She argued that Herbert Marcuse's critical theory, particularly in One Dimensional Man, analyses how advanced industrial societies eliminate oppositional thought by absorbing critique into commodified culture and generating a false consciousness of contentment.

en: Il a soutenu que la théorie psychanalytique lacanienne reconceptualise l'inconscient à travers la linguistique structuraliste, soutenant que l'inconscient est structuré comme un langage et que le désir est toujours le désir de l'Autre médiatisé par l'ordre symbolique.
hint: He maintained that Lacanian psychoanalytic theory reconceptualises the unconscious through structuralist linguistics holding that the unconscious is structured like a language and that desire is always the desire of the Other mediated through the symbolic order.
answers: He maintained that Lacanian psychoanalytic theory reconceptualises the unconscious through structuralist linguistics holding that the unconscious is structured like a language and that desire is always the desire of the Other mediated through the symbolic order.

en: Le structuralisme de Claude Lévi-Strauss applique la linguistique saussurienne à l'anthropologie, soutenant que les phénomènes culturels comme les mythes, les systèmes de parenté et les rituels sont structurés par des oppositions binaires inconscientes universelles à travers les cultures.
hint: The structuralism of Claude Lévi-Strauss applies Saussurean linguistics to anthropology holding that cultural phenomena like myths kinship systems and rituals are structured by unconscious binary oppositions that are universal across cultures.
answers: The structuralism of Claude Lévi-Strauss applies Saussurean linguistics to anthropology holding that cultural phenomena like myths kinship systems and rituals are structured by unconscious binary oppositions that are universal across cultures.

en: Elle a soutenu que la linguistique structuraliste de Saussure distingue entre la langue le système abstrait du langage et la parole son instantiation concrète dans le discours, et soutient que les signes linguistiques sont arbitraires avec le sens produit par la différence au sein du système.
hint: She contended that Saussure's structuralist linguistics distinguishes between langue the abstract system of language and parole its concrete instantiation in speech and holds that linguistic signs are arbitrary with meaning produced through difference within the system.
answers: She contended that Saussure's structuralist linguistics distinguishes between langue the abstract system of language and parole its concrete instantiation in speech and holds that linguistic signs are arbitrary with meaning produced through difference within the system.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie de l'économie débat si les théories économiques sont de véritables explications de la réalité sociale ou des constructions idéologiques et si la discipline doit viser une science positive sans valeurs ou une analyse normative reconnaissant des engagements de valeurs.
hint: He argued that the philosophy of economics debates whether economic theories are genuine explanations of social reality or ideological constructs and whether the discipline should aim for positive value-free science or normative analysis acknowledging value commitments.
answers: He argued that the philosophy of economics debates whether economic theories are genuine explanations of social reality or ideological constructs and whether the discipline should aim for positive value-free science or normative analysis acknowledging value commitments.

en: Elle a soutenu que la théorie de la décision, combinant la théorie des probabilités et la théorie de l'utilité, analyse le choix rationnel sous incertitude soutenant qu'un agent rationnel devrait maximiser l'utilité espérée bien que les critiques d'Ellsberg et Allais défient ce cadre.
hint: She maintained that decision theory, combining probability theory and utility theory, analyses rational choice under uncertainty holding that a rational agent should maximise expected utility though critiques from Ellsberg and Allais challenge this framework.
answers: She maintained that decision theory, combining probability theory and utility theory, analyses rational choice under uncertainty holding that a rational agent should maximise expected utility though critiques from Ellsberg and Allais challenge this framework.

en: Il a soutenu que le paradoxe sorite ou paradoxe du tas démontre que le vague dans le langage naturel génère des puzzles logiques parce que des chaînes de petits incréments mènent d'instances claires à des non-instances claires sans frontière déterminée.
hint: He contended that the Sorites paradox or paradox of the heap demonstrates that vagueness in natural language generates logical puzzles because chains of small increments lead from clear instances to clear non-instances without any determinate boundary.
answers: He contended that the Sorites paradox or paradox of the heap demonstrates that vagueness in natural language generates logical puzzles because chains of small increments lead from clear instances to clear non-instances without any determinate boundary.

en: Le paradoxe du menteur, qui énonce cette phrase est fausse, révèle des tensions fondamentales au cœur des théories formelles de la vérité et a motivé Tarski à développer sa théorie sémantique de la vérité distinguant le langage objet du métalangage.
hint: The liar paradox, which states this sentence is false, reveals fundamental tensions at the heart of formal theories of truth and motivated Tarski to develop his semantic theory of truth distinguishing object language from metalanguage.
answers: The liar paradox, which states this sentence is false, reveals fundamental tensions at the heart of formal theories of truth and motivated Tarski to develop his semantic theory of truth distinguishing object language from metalanguage.

en: Elle a soutenu que les paradoxes de Zénon sur le mouvement, particulièrement la dichotomie et Achille et la tortue, ont confronté les penseurs grecs anciens à la relation entre la divisibilité infinie de l'espace et du temps et la possibilité du mouvement.
hint: She argued that Zeno's paradoxes of motion, particularly the dichotomy and Achilles and the tortoise, challenged ancient Greek thinkers to grapple with the relationship between infinite divisibility of space and time and the possibility of motion.
answers: She argued that Zeno's paradoxes of motion, particularly the dichotomy and Achilles and the tortoise, challenged ancient Greek thinkers to grapple with the relationship between infinite divisibility of space and time and the possibility of motion.

en: Il a soutenu que le paradoxe de Simpson illustre qu'une tendance statistique peut apparaître ou s'inverser lorsque les données sont agrégées ou désagrégées, révélant l'importance de considérer les variables confondantes et le niveau d'analyse dans l'inférence causale.
hint: He maintained that Simpson's paradox illustrates that a statistical trend can appear or reverse when data is aggregated or disaggregated revealing the importance of considering confounding variables and the level of analysis in causal inference.
answers: He maintained that Simpson's paradox illustrates that a statistical trend can appear or reverse when data is aggregated or disaggregated revealing the importance of considering confounding variables and the level of analysis in causal inference.

en: Elle a soutenu que la philosophie de l'action doit expliquer ce qui distingue une action d'un simple événement et comment les raisons sont liées aux causes, avec l'argument influent de Davidson que les raisons sont des causes données sous une certaine description.
hint: She contended that the philosophy of action must explain what distinguishes an action from a mere event and how reasons relate to causes with Davidson's influential argument that reasons are causes given in a certain description.
answers: She contended that the philosophy of action must explain what distinguishes an action from a mere event and how reasons relate to causes with Davidson's influential argument that reasons are causes given in a certain description.

en: Le concept de faiblesse de la volonté ou akrasie, analysé depuis Aristote, décrit le phénomène déroutant de connaître ce qui est le mieux mais d'agir contre son meilleur jugement, soulevant des questions fondamentales sur la rationalité pratique et l'autocontrôle.
hint: The concept of weakness of will or akrasia, analysed since Aristotle, describes the puzzling phenomenon of knowing what is best but acting against one's better judgment provoking fundamental questions about practical rationality and self-control.
answers: The concept of weakness of will or akrasia, analysed since Aristotle, describes the puzzling phenomenon of knowing what is best but acting against one's better judgment provoking fundamental questions about practical rationality and self-control.

en: Il a soutenu que la sagesse pratique ou phronésis dans l'éthique aristotélicienne n'est pas une simple compétence technique mais une vertu intellectuelle fondamentale qui perçoit les traits moralement saillants des situations particulières et délibère bien sur ce que ferait la personne vertueuse.
hint: He argued that practical wisdom or phronesis in Aristotle's ethics is not a mere technical skill but a fundamental intellectual virtue that perceives the morally salient features of particular situations and deliberates well about what the virtuous person would do.
answers: He argued that practical wisdom or phronesis in Aristotle's ethics is not a mere technical skill but a fundamental intellectual virtue that perceives the morally salient features of particular situations and deliberates well about what the virtuous person would do.

en: Elle a examiné comment la philosophie du temps affronte le problème du passage temporel et le statut ontologique du passé du présent et du futur, l'éternalisme soutenant que tous les moments temporels sont également réels et le présentisme soutenant que seul le présent existe.
hint: She examined how the philosophy of time confronts the problem of temporal passage and the ontological status of past present and future with eternalism holding all temporal moments equally real and presentism holding only the present exists.
answers: She examined how the philosophy of time confronts the problem of temporal passage and the ontological status of past present and future with eternalism holding all temporal moments equally real and presentism holding only the present exists.

en: Il a soutenu que le réalisme modal de David Lewis, soutenant que les mondes possibles sont des univers concrets également réels, fournit un cadre élégant pour analyser la modalité mais est ontologiquement extravagant, requérant un engagement radical envers des mondes parallèles infinis.
hint: He contended that the modal realism of David Lewis, holding that possible worlds are equally real concrete universes, provides an elegant framework for analysing modality but is ontologically extravagant requiring a radical commitment to infinite parallel worlds.
answers: He contended that the modal realism of David Lewis, holding that possible worlds are equally real concrete universes, provides an elegant framework for analysing modality but is ontologically extravagant requiring a radical commitment to infinite parallel worlds.

en: Le concept de méréologie, l'étude des relations partie-tout, confronte des questions fondamentales sur le moment où les parties composent un tout et les propriétés que les touts ont par rapport à leurs parties, soulevant des puzzles comme le bateau de Thésée et l'identité personnelle.
hint: The concept of mereology, the study of part-whole relations, confronts fundamental questions about when parts compose a whole and what properties wholes have relative to their parts raising puzzles like the ship of Theseus and personal identity.
answers: The concept of mereology, the study of part-whole relations, confronts fundamental questions about when parts compose a whole and what properties wholes have relative to their parts raising puzzles like the ship of Theseus and personal identity.

en: Elle a soutenu que le problème de Gettier, introduit en 1963, a dévasté l'analyse de la connaissance comme croyance vraie justifiée en construisant des cas où un agent a une croyance vraie justifiée mais manque clairement de connaissance, exigeant une quatrième condition ou une analyse entièrement différente.
hint: She argued that the Gettier problem, introduced in 1963, devastated the justified true belief analysis of knowledge by constructing cases where an agent has justified true belief yet clearly lacks knowledge demanding a fourth condition or an entirely different analysis.
answers: She argued that the Gettier problem, introduced in 1963, devastated the justified true belief analysis of knowledge by constructing cases where an agent has justified true belief yet clearly lacks knowledge demanding a fourth condition or an entirely different analysis.

en: Il a soutenu que l'épistémologie des vertus, développée par Sosa, Zagzebski et Greco, recentre l'évaluation épistémique primaire des croyances vers les agents et leurs vertus intellectuelles, proposant que la connaissance est une croyance vraie issue de l'exercice de la vertu intellectuelle.
hint: He maintained that virtue epistemology, developed by Sosa Zagzebski and Greco, relocates the primary epistemic evaluation from beliefs to agents and their intellectual virtues proposing that knowledge is true belief arising from the exercise of intellectual virtue.
answers: He maintained that virtue epistemology, developed by Sosa Zagzebski and Greco, relocates the primary epistemic evaluation from beliefs to agents and their intellectual virtues proposing that knowledge is true belief arising from the exercise of intellectual virtue.

en: Elle a soutenu que le débat en philosophie des sciences entre réalisme scientifique et anti-réalisme se centre sur la question de savoir si nos meilleures théories scientifiques sont approximativement vraies et si les entités théoriques qu'elles postulent existent réellement au-delà du niveau observationnel.
hint: She contended that the philosophy of science debate between scientific realism and anti-realism centres on whether our best scientific theories are approximately true and whether theoretical entities they posit actually exist beyond the observational level.
answers: She contended that the philosophy of science debate between scientific realism and anti-realism centres on whether our best scientific theories are approximately true and whether theoretical entities they posit actually exist beyond the observational level.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de paradigme, central à la philosophie des sciences de Thomas Kuhn, décrit la constellation d'hypothèses, de méthodes et de problèmes exemplaires qui définissent la pratique d'une communauté scientifique et que les changements de paradigme se produisent par un progrès révolutionnaire plutôt que cumulatif.
hint: He argued that the concept of paradigm, central to Thomas Kuhn's philosophy of science, describes the constellation of assumptions methods and exemplary problems that define a scientific community's practice and that paradigm shifts occur through revolutionary rather than cumulative progress.
answers: He argued that the concept of paradigm, central to Thomas Kuhn's philosophy of science, describes the constellation of assumptions methods and exemplary problems that define a scientific community's practice and that paradigm shifts occur through revolutionary rather than cumulative progress.

en: Elle a soutenu que la méthodologie des programmes de recherche scientifique d'Imre Lakatos offre une alternative plus sophistiquée au falsificationnisme de Popper et aux changements de paradigme de Kuhn, en analysant comment les programmes de recherche sont protégés par des hypothèses auxiliaires et peuvent être progressifs ou dégénérés.
hint: She maintained that Imre Lakatos's methodology of scientific research programmes offers a more sophisticated alternative to both Popper's falsificationism and Kuhn's paradigm shifts by analysing how research programmes are protected by auxiliary hypotheses and can be progressive or degenerating.
answers: She maintained that Imre Lakatos's methodology of scientific research programmes offers a more sophisticated alternative to both Popper's falsificationism and Kuhn's paradigm shifts by analysing how research programmes are protected by auxiliary hypotheses and can be progressive or degenerating.

en: Il a soutenu que l'anarchisme épistémologique de Paul Feyerabend, exprimé dans Contre la méthode, soutient qu'il n'y a pas de méthode scientifique unique suivie de façon cohérente dans l'histoire des sciences et que le pluralisme méthodologique facilite le progrès scientifique.
hint: He contended that Paul Feyerabend's epistemological anarchism, expressed in Against Method, holds that there is no single scientific method that has been consistently followed in the history of science and that methodological pluralism facilitates scientific progress.
answers: He contended that Paul Feyerabend's epistemological anarchism, expressed in Against Method, holds that there is no single scientific method that has been consistently followed in the history of science and that methodological pluralism facilitates scientific progress.

en: Le concept de supervenance en philosophie de l'esprit soutient que les propriétés mentales supervisent sur les propriétés physiques, signifiant qu'il ne peut y avoir de différence mentale sans différence physique bien que cela laisse ouverts des questions sur la réduction et l'efficacité causale.
hint: The concept of supervenience in philosophy of mind holds that mental properties supervene on physical properties meaning that there can be no mental difference without a physical difference though this leaves open questions about reduction and causal efficacy.
answers: The concept of supervenience in philosophy of mind holds that mental properties supervene on physical properties meaning that there can be no mental difference without a physical difference though this leaves open questions about reduction and causal efficacy.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de qualia, le caractère qualitatif subjectif de l'expérience comme l'effet que cela fait de voir le rouge, pose le défi le plus sérieux aux comptes physicalistes de l'esprit car il semble résister à toute explication fonctionnelle ou physique.
hint: She argued that the concept of qualia, the subjective qualitative character of experience such as what it is like to see red, poses the most serious challenge to physicalist accounts of mind because it seems to resist any functional or physical explanation.
answers: She argued that the concept of qualia, the subjective qualitative character of experience such as what it is like to see red, poses the most serious challenge to physicalist accounts of mind because it seems to resist any functional or physical explanation.

en: Il a soutenu que l'argument célèbre de Thomas Nagel qu'il y a quelque chose que cela fait d'être une chauve-souris démontre que l'expérience subjective ne peut être entièrement capturée par une description physique objective, posant le défi fondamental de la conscience au physicalisme.
hint: He maintained that Thomas Nagel's famous argument that there is something it is like to be a bat demonstrates that subjective experience cannot be fully captured by objective physical description posing the fundamental challenge of consciousness to physicalism.
answers: He maintained that Thomas Nagel's famous argument that there is something it is like to be a bat demonstrates that subjective experience cannot be fully captured by objective physical description posing the fundamental challenge of consciousness to physicalism.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept philosophique de conscience soulève le problème difficile distingué par David Chalmers des problèmes faciles, le problème difficile étant pourquoi et comment les processus physiques donnent naissance à l'expérience subjective.
hint: She contended that the philosophical concept of consciousness raises the hard problem distinguished by David Chalmers from easy problems the hard problem being why and how physical processes give rise to subjective experience at all.
answers: She contended that the philosophical concept of consciousness raises the hard problem distinguished by David Chalmers from easy problems the hard problem being why and how physical processes give rise to subjective experience at all.

en: Il a soutenu que le débat en philosophie du langage entre l'externalisme et l'internalisme sémantiques porte sur la question de savoir si les significations des termes des genres naturels sont déterminées par des facteurs dans l'environnement et la communauté linguistique ou seulement par les états mentaux du locuteur individuel.
hint: He argued that the philosophy of language debate between semantic externalism and internalism concerns whether the meanings of natural kind terms are determined by factors in the environment and the linguistic community or solely by the mental states of the individual speaker.
answers: He argued that the philosophy of language debate between semantic externalism and internalism concerns whether the meanings of natural kind terms are determined by factors in the environment and the linguistic community or solely by the mental states of the individual speaker.

en: Elle a soutenu que la critique de Kripke des théories descriptivistes de la référence soutient que les noms propres et les termes des genres naturels sont des désignateurs rigides qui réfèrent au même objet ou genre dans tous les mondes possibles indépendamment des descriptions que les locuteurs leur associent.
hint: She maintained that Kripke's critique of descriptivist theories of reference holds that proper names and natural kind terms are rigid designators that refer to the same object or kind in all possible worlds regardless of the descriptions speakers associate with them.
answers: She maintained that Kripke's critique of descriptivist theories of reference holds that proper names and natural kind terms are rigid designators that refer to the same object or kind in all possible worlds regardless of the descriptions speakers associate with them.

en: Il a soutenu que l'analyse philosophique du témoignage comme source de connaissance soulève la question de savoir si nous sommes épistémiquement habilités à croire ce que les autres nous disent par défaut, via le réductionnisme exigeant une justification indépendante ou via le non-réductionnisme permettant une habilitation par défaut.
hint: He contended that the philosophical analysis of testimony as a source of knowledge raises the question of whether we are epistemically entitled to believe what others tell us by default through reductionism demanding independent justification or through non-reductionism allowing default entitlement.
answers: He contended that the philosophical analysis of testimony as a source of knowledge raises the question of whether we are epistemically entitled to believe what others tell us by default through reductionism demanding independent justification or through non-reductionism allowing default entitlement.

en: Le concept d'abduction ou inférence à la meilleure explication, analysé par Peirce et développé par Harman et Lipton, soutient que nous sommes épistémiquement justifiés à inférer l'hypothèse qui expliquerait le mieux les preuves disponibles même lorsqu'elle n'en est pas strictement entailée.
hint: The concept of abduction or inference to the best explanation, analysed by Peirce and developed by Harman and Lipton, holds that we are epistemically justified in inferring the hypothesis that would best explain the available evidence even when not strictly entailed by it.
answers: The concept of abduction or inference to the best explanation, analysed by Peirce and developed by Harman and Lipton, holds that we are epistemically justified in inferring the hypothesis that would best explain the available evidence even when not strictly entailed by it.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de biais implicite, étudié en psychologie sociale et en philosophie, décrit des attitudes ou des stéréotypes inconscients qui influencent le jugement et le comportement de façon à pouvoir perpétuer la discrimination même chez des individus explicitement engagés pour l'égalité.
hint: She argued that the concept of implicit bias, extensively studied in social psychology and philosophy, describes unconscious attitudes or stereotypes that influence judgment and behaviour in ways that can perpetuate discrimination even among individuals explicitly committed to equality.
answers: She argued that the concept of implicit bias, extensively studied in social psychology and philosophy, describes unconscious attitudes or stereotypes that influence judgment and behaviour in ways that can perpetuate discrimination even among individuals explicitly committed to equality.

en: Il a soutenu que l'analyse philosophique de la race comme construction sociale versus réalité biologique révèle que la race manque d'un fondement biologique cohérent mais reste une réalité sociale et politique puissante avec des conséquences matérielles profondes.
hint: He maintained that the philosophical analysis of race as a social construction versus a biological reality reveals that race lacks a coherent biological foundation but remains a powerful social and political reality with deep material consequences.
answers: He maintained that the philosophical analysis of race as a social construction versus a biological reality reveals that race lacks a coherent biological foundation but remains a powerful social and political reality with deep material consequences.

en: Le concept de racisme structurel, distingué du préjugé individuel, décrit comment les institutions sociales, les politiques et les pratiques produisent des résultats racialement disparates qui perpétuent l'inégalité raciale même en l'absence d'intention raciste individuelle.
hint: The concept of structural racism, distinguished from individual prejudice, describes how social institutions policies and practices produce racially disparate outcomes that perpetuate racial inequality even in the absence of individual racist intent.
answers: The concept of structural racism, distinguished from individual prejudice, describes how social institutions policies and practices produce racially disparate outcomes that perpetuate racial inequality even in the absence of individual racist intent.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept philosophique de solidarité, examiné par Rorty et d'autres, décrit une forme de motivation morale qui ne requiert pas un fondement universel mais étend la loyauté et le souci dans des cercles expansifs partant de la vulnérabilité partagée et de l'identification contingente.
hint: She contended that the philosophical concept of solidarity, examined by Rorty and others, describes a form of moral motivation that does not require universal grounding but extends loyalty and concern in expanding circles beginning from shared vulnerability and contingent identification.
answers: She contended that the philosophical concept of solidarity, examined by Rorty and others, describes a form of moral motivation that does not require universal grounding but extends loyalty and concern in expanding circles beginning from shared vulnerability and contingent identification.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de légitimité politique en philosophie contemporaine requiert plus qu'un simple pouvoir coercitif et implique une combinaison d'équité procédurale, de consentement rationnel, de justifiabilité normative et d'approbation réflexive par ceux qui sont soumis à l'autorité politique.
hint: He argued that the concept of political legitimacy in contemporary philosophy requires more than mere coercive power and involves some combination of procedural fairness rational consent normative justifiability and reflective endorsement by those subject to political authority.
answers: He argued that the concept of political legitimacy in contemporary philosophy requires more than mere coercive power and involves some combination of procedural fairness rational consent normative justifiability and reflective endorsement by those subject to political authority.

en: Le concept d'autodétermination en philosophie politique débat si elle s'applique principalement aux individus permettant l'autonomie personnelle ou aux collectivités permettant aux communautés nationales et culturelles de se gouverner, créant des tensions entre le libéralisme individualiste et le communautarisme.
hint: The concept of self-determination in political philosophy debates whether it applies primarily to individuals enabling personal autonomy or to collectivities enabling national and cultural communities to govern themselves creating tensions between liberal individualism and communitarianism.
answers: The concept of self-determination in political philosophy debates whether it applies primarily to individuals enabling personal autonomy or to collectivities enabling national and cultural communities to govern themselves creating tensions between liberal individualism and communitarianism.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept philosophique d'aliénation chez Marx étend l'analyse de Hegel pour décrire l'estrangement du travailleur par rapport au produit du travail, à l'acte de production, à son être générique et aux autres êtres humains comme conséquence des relations de marchandise capitalistes.
hint: She maintained that the philosophical concept of alienation in Marx extends Hegel's analysis to describe the worker's estrangement from the product of labour the act of production their species-being and from other human beings as a consequence of capitalist commodity relations.
answers: She maintained that the philosophical concept of alienation in Marx extends Hegel's analysis to describe the worker's estrangement from the product of labour the act of production their species-being and from other human beings as a consequence of capitalist commodity relations.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de critique de l'idéologie dans la tradition de l'École de Francfort analyse comment les idées dominantes légitiment les relations de pouvoir existantes en faisant paraître naturels, inévitables et universels des arrangements historiquement contingents, désactivant ainsi la conscience émancipatrice.

answers: He contended that the concept of ideology critique in the Frankfurt School tradition analyses how dominant ideas legitimate existing power relations by making historically contingent arrangements appear natural inevitable and universal thereby disabling emancipatory consciousness.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'hégémonie dans la théorie politique de Gramsci décrit comment les classes dirigeantes maintiennent la domination non pas principalement par la coercition mais par le leadership intellectuel et moral gagnant le consentement actif des dominés à travers les institutions de la société civile.
hint: She argued that the concept of hegemony in Gramsci's political theory describes how ruling classes maintain dominance not primarily through coercion but through intellectual and moral leadership winning the active consent of the dominated through civil society institutions.
answers: She argued that the concept of hegemony in Gramsci's political theory describes how ruling classes maintain dominance not primarily through coercion but through intellectual and moral leadership winning the active consent of the dominated through civil society institutions.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de désobéissance civile, analysé par Thoreau, King et Rawls, décrit une violation publique non violente de la loi visant à changer des lois ou politiques injustes lorsque les autres moyens ont été épuisés, faisant appel au sens de la justice de la majorité.
hint: He maintained that the concept of civil disobedience, analysed by Thoreau King and Rawls, describes non-violent public breach of law aimed at changing unjust laws or policies when other means have been exhausted appealing to the sense of justice of the majority.
answers: He maintained that the concept of civil disobedience, analysed by Thoreau King and Rawls, describes non-violent public breach of law aimed at changing unjust laws or policies when other means have been exhausted appealing to the sense of justice of the majority.

en: Le concept de liberté négative dans les deux concepts de liberté d'Isaiah Berlin décrit la liberté comme la non-interférence avec le choix individuel, définissant la liberté comme l'absence d'obstacles externes ou de coercitions et la contrastant avec la liberté positive comme maîtrise de soi.
hint: The concept of negative liberty in Isaiah Berlin's two concepts of liberty describes freedom as non-interference with individual choice defining freedom as the absence of external obstacles or coercions and contrasting it with positive liberty as self-mastery.
answers: The concept of negative liberty in Isaiah Berlin's two concepts of liberty describes freedom as non-interference with individual choice defining freedom as the absence of external obstacles or coercions and contrasting it with positive liberty as self-mastery.

en: Elle a soutenu que la liberté républicaine, ravivée par Pettit et Skinner, est distincte des libertés négative et positive, soutenant que la liberté requiert non seulement l'absence d'interférence mais l'absence de domination signifiant une non-sujétion sécurisée au pouvoir arbitraire.
hint: She argued that republican liberty, revived by Pettit and Skinner, is distinct from both negative liberty and positive liberty holding that freedom requires not merely absence of interference but absence of domination meaning secure non-subjection to arbitrary power.
answers: She argued that republican liberty, revived by Pettit and Skinner, is distinct from both negative liberty and positive liberty holding that freedom requires not merely absence of interference but absence of domination meaning secure non-subjection to arbitrary power.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept des droits humains fait face à des questions philosophiques profondes sur leurs fondements, leur justification et leur portée, avec des approches de droit naturel, contractariennes, kantiennes et pragmatistes offrant toutes des réponses différentes sur la raison pour laquelle nous avons des droits.
hint: He contended that the concept of human rights faces deep philosophical questions about their foundation justification and scope with natural law contractarian Kantian and pragmatist approaches all offering different answers to why we have rights.
answers: He contended that the concept of human rights faces deep philosophical questions about their foundation justification and scope with natural law contractarian Kantian and pragmatist approaches all offering different answers to why we have rights.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de gouvernance mondiale décrit les cadres institutionnels multi-niveaux les traités les normes et les pratiques par lesquels les États les organisations internationales la société civile et d'autres acteurs coordonnent l'action sur les défis transnationaux en l'absence d'un gouvernement mondial.
hint: She maintained that the concept of global governance describes the multi-level institutional frameworks treaties norms and practices through which states international organisations civil society and other actors coordinate action on transnational challenges lacking a world government.
answers: She maintained that the concept of global governance describes the multi-level institutional frameworks treaties norms and practices through which states international organisations civil society and other actors coordinate action on transnational challenges lacking a world government.

en: Il a soutenu que l'analyse philosophique de la souveraineté dans le système international révèle une tension profonde entre la norme westphalienne de non-ingérence et la doctrine émergente de la responsabilité de protéger qui soutient que la souveraineté est conditionnelle à la protection des citoyens.
hint: He argued that the philosophical analysis of sovereignty in the international system reveals a deep tension between the Westphalian norm of non-interference and the emerging doctrine of responsibility to protect which holds that sovereignty is conditional on protecting citizens.
answers: He argued that the philosophical analysis of sovereignty in the international system reveals a deep tension between the Westphalian norm of non-interference and the emerging doctrine of responsibility to protect which holds that sovereignty is conditional on protecting citizens.

en: Le concept de cosmopolitisme en philosophie politique soutient que les êtres humains ont des obligations morales envers tous les autres êtres humains indépendamment des frontières nationales et plaide pour des institutions mondiales suffisamment robustes pour protéger les droits humains universels et lutter contre l'injustice mondiale.
hint: The concept of cosmopolitanism in political philosophy holds that human beings have moral obligations to all other human beings regardless of national boundaries and argues for global institutions robust enough to protect universal human rights and address global injustice.
answers: The concept of cosmopolitanism in political philosophy holds that human beings have moral obligations to all other human beings regardless of national boundaries and argues for global institutions robust enough to protect universal human rights and address global injustice.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de nationalisme en philosophie politique soulève des questions sur la question de savoir si les identités nationales constituent des communautés moralement significatives capables de fonder des obligations spéciales et si l'autodétermination nationale est un droit fondamental.
hint: She contended that the concept of nationalism in political philosophy raises questions about whether national identities constitute morally significant communities capable of grounding special obligations and whether national self-determination is a fundamental right.
answers: She contended that the concept of nationalism in political philosophy raises questions about whether national identities constitute morally significant communities capable of grounding special obligations and whether national self-determination is a fundamental right.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de pluralisme en philosophie politique décrit la diversité irréductible des valeurs des modes de vie et des conceptions du bien dans les sociétés modernes et soulève la question de la façon dont les sociétés libérales peuvent accommoder cette diversité sans imposer une conception unique.
hint: He maintained that the concept of pluralism in political philosophy describes the irreducible diversity of values ways of life and conceptions of the good in modern societies and raises the question of how liberal societies can accommodate this diversity without imposing a single conception.
answers: He maintained that the concept of pluralism in political philosophy describes the irreducible diversity of values ways of life and conceptions of the good in modern societies and raises the question of how liberal societies can accommodate this diversity without imposing a single conception.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de multiculturalisme comme théorie politique avancée par Kymlicka soutient que les démocraties libérales devraient fournir des droits et protections spéciaux pour les minorités culturelles pour permettre leur épanouissement continu sans exiger l'assimilation dans la culture majoritaire.
hint: She argued that the concept of multiculturalism as political theory advanced by Kymlicka holds that liberal democracies should provide special rights and protections for cultural minorities to enable their continued flourishing without demanding assimilation into the majority culture.
answers: She argued that the concept of multiculturalism as political theory advanced by Kymlicka holds that liberal democracies should provide special rights and protections for cultural minorities to enable their continued flourishing without demanding assimilation into the majority culture.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie de l'éducation examine la finalité de l'éducation en débattant si elle vise la transmission du patrimoine culturel le développement de l'agence rationnelle autonome la cultivation de la citoyenneté démocratique ou la libération des opprimés comme le soutient Paulo Freire.
hint: He contended that the philosophy of education examines what education is for debating whether it aims at the transmission of cultural heritage the development of autonomous rational agency the cultivation of democratic citizenship or the liberation of the oppressed as Paulo Freire argued.
answers: He contended that the philosophy of education examines what education is for debating whether it aims at the transmission of cultural heritage the development of autonomous rational agency the cultivation of democratic citizenship or the liberation of the oppressed as Paulo Freire argued.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de sphère publique, théorisé par Habermas, décrit un espace de vie sociale où les individus privés peuvent se rassembler pour discuter des questions d'intérêt public formant une opinion publique pouvant défier le pouvoir de l'État mais qui a été de plus en plus colonisée par les médias et les intérêts corporatifs.
hint: She maintained that the concept of the public sphere, theorised by Habermas, describes a realm of social life where private individuals can assemble to discuss matters of public concern forming public opinion that can challenge state power but which has been increasingly colonised by media and corporate interests.
answers: She maintained that the concept of the public sphere, theorised by Habermas, describes a realm of social life where private individuals can assemble to discuss matters of public concern forming public opinion that can challenge state power but which has been increasingly colonised by media and corporate interests.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'action communicative dans la théorie de Habermas décrit une action orientée vers la compréhension mutuelle à travers le dialogue gouverné par des prétentions de validité de vérité d'authenticité et de justesse normative contrasté avec l'action stratégique orientée vers le succès.
hint: He argued that the concept of communicative action in Habermas's theory describes action oriented towards mutual understanding through dialogue governed by validity claims of truth truthfulness and normative rightness contrasted with strategic action oriented towards success.
answers: He argued that the concept of communicative action in Habermas's theory describes action oriented towards mutual understanding through dialogue governed by validity claims of truth truthfulness and normative rightness contrasted with strategic action oriented towards success.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de colonisation du monde vécu dans la théorie critique de Habermas décrit le processus par lequel les médias directeurs de l'argent et du pouvoir envahissent et remplacent l'action communicative dans les domaines sociaux qui en ont besoin comme la famille l'éducation et la culture.
hint: She contended that the concept of lifeworld colonisation in Habermas's critical theory describes the process by which the steering media of money and power invade and replace communicative action in social domains that require it such as family education and culture.
answers: She contended that the concept of lifeworld colonisation in Habermas's critical theory describes the process by which the steering media of money and power invade and replace communicative action in social domains that require it such as family education and culture.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept philosophique de réification, développé par Lukacs à partir de Marx, décrit le processus par lequel les relations sociales et les qualités humaines sont transformées en propriétés semblables à des choses qui apparaissent naturelles et inévitables plutôt que contingentes historiquement.
hint: He maintained that the philosophical concept of reification, developed by Lukacs building on Marx, describes the process by which social relations and human qualities are transformed into thing-like properties that appear as natural and inevitable rather than historically contingent human creations.
answers: He maintained that the philosophical concept of reification, developed by Lukacs building on Marx, describes the process by which social relations and human qualities are transformed into thing-like properties that appear as natural and inevitable rather than historically contingent human creations.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de matérialisme dialectique comme méthode philosophique du marxisme soutient que la réalité sociale se développe à travers le choc des contradictions au niveau matériel des forces productives et des rapports de production, moteur du changement historique.
hint: She argued that the concept of dialectical materialism as the philosophical method of Marxism holds that social reality develops through the clash of contradictions at the material level of productive forces and relations of production driving historical change.
answers: She argued that the concept of dialectical materialism as the philosophical method of Marxism holds that social reality develops through the clash of contradictions at the material level of productive forces and relations of production driving historical change.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de reproduction en théorie sociale, examiné par Bourdieu et d'autres, révèle que les inégalités sociales sont perpétuées non seulement par les structures économiques mais par le capital culturel, la violence symbolique et la transmission des dispositions à travers le système éducatif.
hint: He contended that the concept of reproduction in social theory, examined by Bourdieu and others, reveals that social inequalities are perpetuated not only by economic structures but by cultural capital symbolic violence and the transmission of dispositions through the educational system.
answers: He contended that the concept of reproduction in social theory, examined by Bourdieu and others, reveals that social inequalities are perpetuated not only by economic structures but by cultural capital symbolic violence and the transmission of dispositions through the educational system.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de pouvoir symbolique dans la sociologie de Bourdieu décrit un pouvoir qui opère à travers la méconnaissance de son caractère arbitraire rendant les agents dominés complices de leur propre domination en internalisant les dispositions qui reproduisent l'ordre social.
hint: She maintained that the concept of symbolic power in Bourdieu's sociology describes power that operates through the misrecognition of its arbitrary character making dominated agents complicit in their own domination by internalising the dispositions that reproduce the social order.
answers: She maintained that the concept of symbolic power in Bourdieu's sociology describes power that operates through the misrecognition of its arbitrary character making dominated agents complicit in their own domination by internalising the dispositions that reproduce the social order.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de champ dans la théorie sociale de Bourdieu décrit un espace social relativement autonome avec ses propres règles enjeux et formes de capital dans lequel les agents se disputent des formes spécifiques de capital et de position générant des luttes qui reproduisent ou transforment le champ.
hint: He argued that the concept of field in Bourdieu's social theory describes a relatively autonomous social space with its own rules stakes and forms of capital in which agents compete for specific forms of capital and position generating struggles that reproduce or transform the field.
answers: He argued that the concept of field in Bourdieu's social theory describes a relatively autonomous social space with its own rules stakes and forms of capital in which agents compete for specific forms of capital and position generating struggles that reproduce or transform the field.

en: Le concept de discours dans l'analyse généalogique de Foucault ne se réfère pas simplement au langage mais aux pratiques régulées par lesquelles des objets, des sujets et des vérités sont produits et qui exercent du pouvoir en déterminant ce qui peut être dit et su dans une période historique donnée.
hint: The concept of discourse in Foucault's genealogical analysis does not refer merely to language but to the regulated practices through which objects subjects and truths are produced and which exercise power by determining what can be said and known in a given historical period.
answers: The concept of discourse in Foucault's genealogical analysis does not refer merely to language but to the regulated practices through which objects subjects and truths are produced and which exercise power by determining what can be said and known in a given historical period.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de résistance dans la pensée post-structuraliste, s'appuyant sur Foucault et Deleuze, soutient que la résistance est immanente au pouvoir et ne requiert pas une position en dehors de lui, signifiant que le pouvoir est toujours déjà accompagné de possibilités de résistance et de contre-conduite.
hint: She contended that the concept of resistance in post-structuralist thought, drawing on Foucault and Deleuze, holds that resistance is immanent to power and does not require a position outside it meaning that power is always already accompanied by possibilities of resistance and counter-conduct.
answers: She contended that the concept of resistance in post-structuralist thought, drawing on Foucault and Deleuze, holds that resistance is immanent to power and does not require a position outside it meaning that power is always already accompanied by possibilities of resistance and counter-conduct.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept philosophique de subjectivation chez Foucault décrit le processus paradoxal par lequel les individus sont constitués comme sujets à la fois par des relations de pouvoir externes qui les assujettissent et par des pratiques de soi par lesquelles ils se forment activement.
hint: He argued that the philosophical concept of subjectivation in Foucault describes the paradoxical process by which individuals are constituted as subjects both through external power relations that subject them and through practices of self-formation through which they actively shape themselves.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de rhizome de Deleuze et Guattari, par opposition à l'arbre arborescent, propose un modèle de pensée, de culture et de politique qui est non-hiérarchique, multiple, latéral et résistant aux oppositions binaires et aux identités fixes.
hint: She maintained that Deleuze and Guattari's concept of the rhizome as opposed to the arborescent tree proposes a model of thought culture and politics that is non-hierarchical multiplicitous lateral and resistant to binary oppositions and fixed identities.
