en: Il a soutenu que le concept de déterritorialisation et reterritorialisation chez Deleuze et Guattari décrit comment les flux de désir de capital de culture et de populations échappent constamment aux structures et codifications existantes pour être capturés et reconfigurés par de nouvelles structures.
hint: He contended that the concept of deterritorialisation and reterritorialisation in Deleuze and Guattari describes how flows of desire capital culture and populations constantly escape existing structures and codings only to be captured and reconfigured by new structures.
answers: He contended that the concept of deterritorialisation and reterritorialisation in Deleuze and Guattari describes how flows of desire capital culture and populations constantly escape existing structures and codings only to be captured and reconfigured by new structures.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de biopolitique dans les travaux tardifs de Foucault décrit la technologie gouvernementale qui prend la population comme objet, visant à optimiser la vie de l'espèce à travers des techniques démographiques, statistiques et de santé publique.
hint: She argued that the concept of biopolitics in Foucault's late work describes the governmental technology that takes the population as its object aiming to optimise the life of the species through demographic statistical and public health techniques.
answers: She argued that the concept of biopolitics in Foucault's late work describes the governmental technology that takes the population as its object aiming to optimise the life of the species through demographic statistical and public health techniques.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de nécropolitique, développé par Achille Mbembe étendant Foucault, décrit comment la souveraineté opère de plus en plus à travers le pouvoir de déterminer qui peut vivre et qui doit mourir tel que manifesté dans les régimes coloniaux et raciaux de pouvoir.
hint: He maintained that the concept of necropolitics, developed by Achille Mbembe extending Foucault, describes how sovereignty increasingly operates through the power to determine who may live and who must die as manifested in colonial and racial regimes of power.
answers: He maintained that the concept of necropolitics, developed by Achille Mbembe extending Foucault, describes how sovereignty increasingly operates through the power to determine who may live and who must die as manifested in colonial and racial regimes of power.

en: Le concept de théorie postcoloniale, façonné par Said, Spivak et Bhabha, examine comment les héritages coloniaux continuent à structurer la connaissance, la représentation culturelle, l'économie politique et la subjectivité, défiant l'eurocentrisme dans la production du savoir et exigeant une décolonisation épistémique.
hint: The concept of postcolonial theory, shaped by Said Spivak and Bhabha, examines how colonial legacies continue to structure knowledge cultural representation political economy and subjectivity challenging Eurocentrism in the production of knowledge and demanding epistemic decolonisation.
answers: The concept of postcolonial theory, shaped by Said Spivak and Bhabha, examines how colonial legacies continue to structure knowledge cultural representation political economy and subjectivity challenging Eurocentrism in the production of knowledge and demanding epistemic decolonisation.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'orientalisme d'Edward Said décrit comment les travaux académiques occidentaux sur l'Orient n'étaient pas une représentation objective mais une formation discursive qui a produit un Orient stéréotypé et subordonné servant à légitimer la domination impériale occidentale.
hint: She contended that Edward Said's concept of Orientalism describes how Western scholarship on the East was not objective representation but a discursive formation that produced a stereotyped subordinate Orient serving to legitimate Western imperial domination.
answers: She contended that Edward Said's concept of Orientalism describes how Western scholarship on the East was not objective representation but a discursive formation that produced a stereotyped subordinate Orient serving to legitimate Western imperial domination.

en: Il a soutenu que la célèbre question de Gayatri Spivak les subalternes peuvent-ils parler interroge si ceux aux marges des structures coloniales et capitalistes peuvent articuler leurs perspectives de manières qui sont entendues et validées par les systèmes discursifs dominants.
hint: He argued that Gayatri Spivak's famous question can the subaltern speak interrogates whether those at the margins of colonial and capitalist structures can articulate their perspectives in ways that are heard and validated by dominant discursive systems.
answers: He argued that Gayatri Spivak's famous question can the subaltern speak interrogates whether those at the margins of colonial and capitalist structures can articulate their perspectives in ways that are heard and validated by dominant discursive systems.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'hybridité d'Homi Bhabha dans la théorie du discours colonial décrit les espaces interstitiels créés dans les rencontres coloniales où ni la culture du colonisateur ni celle du colonisé n'est pure mais où un troisième espace de négociation culturelle et d'ambivalence émerge.
hint: She maintained that Homi Bhabha's concept of hybridity in colonial discourse theory describes the in-between spaces created in colonial encounters where neither coloniser nor colonised culture is pure but a third space of cultural negotiation and ambivalence emerges.
answers: She maintained that Homi Bhabha's concept of hybridity in colonial discourse theory describes the in-between spaces created in colonial encounters where neither coloniser nor colonised culture is pure but a third space of cultural negotiation and ambivalence emerges.

en: Il a soutenu que l'analyse philosophique de la technologie dans La Question de la technique de Heidegger soutient que la technologie moderne n'est pas simplement un outil mais un mode de dévoilement qui encastre la nature et les humains comme réserve disponible les réduisant à des ressources pour l'optimisation.
hint: He contended that the philosophical analysis of technology in Heidegger's The Question Concerning Technology argues that modern technology is not merely a tool but a mode of revealing that enframes nature and humans as standing reserve reducing them to resources for optimisation.
answers: He contended that the philosophical analysis of technology in Heidegger's The Question Concerning Technology argues that modern technology is not merely a tool but a mode of revealing that enframes nature and humans as standing reserve reducing them to resources for optimisation.

en: Elle a soutenu que la philosophie de l'intelligence artificielle soulève des questions profondes sur la conscience la compréhension et l'intentionnalité avec l'argument de la chambre chinoise de Searle remettant en question la prétention que les systèmes computationnels symboliques peuvent genuinement comprendre plutôt que simplement simuler la compréhension.
hint: She argued that the philosophy of artificial intelligence raises deep questions about consciousness understanding and intentionality with Searle's Chinese Room argument challenging the claim that symbolic computational systems can genuinely understand rather than merely simulate understanding.
answers: She argued that the philosophy of artificial intelligence raises deep questions about consciousness understanding and intentionality with Searle's Chinese Room argument challenging the claim that symbolic computational systems can genuinely understand rather than merely simulate understanding.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'émergence décrit comment les systèmes complexes présentent des propriétés qui ne peuvent être prédites ni réduites aux propriétés de leurs seuls composants, la conscience étant peut-être l'exemple philosophiquement le plus significatif d'émergence forte.
hint: He maintained that the concept of emergence describes how complex systems exhibit properties that cannot be predicted from or reduced to the properties of their components alone with consciousness perhaps being the most philosophically significant example of strong emergence.
answers: He maintained that the concept of emergence describes how complex systems exhibit properties that cannot be predicted from or reduced to the properties of their components alone with consciousness perhaps being the most philosophically significant example of strong emergence.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de complexité dans la théorie des systèmes remet en question les approches réductionnistes des phénomènes naturels et sociaux, soutenant que les systèmes adaptatifs complexes présentent des dynamiques non linéaires, une sensibilité aux conditions initiales et des propriétés émergentes qui nécessitent de nouveaux cadres explicatifs.
hint: She contended that the concept of complexity in systems theory challenges reductionist approaches to natural and social phenomena arguing that complex adaptive systems exhibit non-linear dynamics sensitivity to initial conditions and emergent properties that require new explanatory frameworks.
answers: She contended that the concept of complexity in systems theory challenges reductionist approaches to natural and social phenomena arguing that complex adaptive systems exhibit non-linear dynamics sensitivity to initial conditions and emergent properties that require new explanatory frameworks.

en: Il a soutenu que l'analyse philosophique de la métaphore développée par Lakoff et Johnson révèle que la métaphore n'est pas simplement un dispositif littéraire mais une structure cognitive fondamentale à travers laquelle nous conceptualisons des domaines abstraits en termes d'expériences incarnées plus concrètes.
hint: He argued that the philosophy of language analysis of metaphor developed by Lakoff and Johnson reveals that metaphor is not merely a literary device but a fundamental cognitive structure through which we conceptualise abstract domains in terms of more concrete embodied experiences.
answers: He argued that the philosophy of language analysis of metaphor developed by Lakoff and Johnson reveals that metaphor is not merely a literary device but a fundamental cognitive structure through which we conceptualise abstract domains in terms of more concrete embodied experiences.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de dissonance cognitive en psychologie et philosophie de l'action décrit l'inconfort résultant de croyances contradictoires ou entre croyance et action et les mécanismes psychologiques par lesquels les individus réduisent cette dissonance.
hint: She maintained that the concept of cognitive dissonance in psychology and philosophy of action describes the discomfort arising from holding contradictory beliefs or between belief and action and the psychological mechanisms through which individuals reduce this dissonance.
answers: She maintained that the concept of cognitive dissonance in psychology and philosophy of action describes the discomfort arising from holding contradictory beliefs or between belief and action and the psychological mechanisms through which individuals reduce this dissonance.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de rationalité limitée introduit par Herbert Simon soutient que la prise de décision humaine ne maximise pas l'utilité espérée mais utilise des heuristiques et satisfait en se contentant de solutions assez bonnes compte tenu des limites cognitives et des coûts d'information.
hint: He contended that the concept of bounded rationality introduced by Herbert Simon holds that human decision-making does not maximise expected utility but uses heuristics and satisfices settling for good enough solutions given cognitive limits and information costs.
answers: He contended that the concept of bounded rationality introduced by Herbert Simon holds that human decision-making does not maximise expected utility but uses heuristics and satisfices settling for good enough solutions given cognitive limits and information costs.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'effets de cadrage en économie comportementale et en épistémologie démontre que la façon dont les options sont décrites influence significativement les choix et les jugements, révélant que la rationalité est plus dépendante du contexte et sujette aux biais que la théorie classique ne l'assume.
hint: She argued that the concept of framing effects in behavioural economics and epistemology demonstrates that the way options are described significantly influences choices and judgments revealing that rationality is more context-dependent and susceptible to bias than classical theory assumes.
answers: She argued that the concept of framing effects in behavioural economics and epistemology demonstrates that the way options are described significantly influences choices and judgments revealing that rationality is more context-dependent and susceptible to bias than classical theory assumes.

en: Il a soutenu que le débat en philosophie de l'esprit sur la causation mentale demande comment les événements mentaux compris comme distincts des événements physiques peuvent avoir une efficacité causale genuine dans la production d'effets physiques sans réduire le mental au physique ni accepter un dualisme implausible.
hint: He maintained that the philosophy of mind debate over mental causation asks how mental events understood as distinct from physical events can have genuine causal efficacy in producing physical effects without either reducing the mental to the physical or accepting an implausible dualism.
answers: He maintained that the philosophy of mind debate over mental causation asks how mental events understood as distinct from physical events can have genuine causal efficacy in producing physical effects without either reducing the mental to the physical or accepting an implausible dualism.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de physicalisme ou matérialisme en philosophie de l'esprit soutient que les états et processus mentaux sont entièrement déterminés par les états et processus physiques mais des débats continuent sur la question de savoir si cela requiert une réduction, une identité ou une simple supervenance.
hint: She contended that the concept of physicalism or materialism in philosophy of mind holds that mental states and processes are fully determined by physical states and processes but debates continue over whether this requires reduction identity or mere supervenience.
answers: She contended that the concept of physicalism or materialism in philosophy of mind holds that mental states and processes are fully determined by physical states and processes but debates continue over whether this requires reduction identity or mere supervenience.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de matérialisme éliminativiste avancé par Paul et Patricia Churchland soutient que la psychologie du sens commun avec ses paroles de croyances désirs et intentions est une théorie radicalement fausse qui sera remplacée par une neuroscience mature sans résidu.
hint: He argued that the concept of eliminative materialism advanced by Paul and Patricia Churchland holds that folk psychology with its talk of beliefs desires and intentions is a radically false theory that will be replaced by a mature neuroscience without remainder.
answers: He argued that the concept of eliminative materialism advanced by Paul and Patricia Churchland holds that folk psychology with its talk of beliefs desires and intentions is a radically false theory that will be replaced by a mature neuroscience without remainder.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de réalisabilité multiple, central au débat sur le fonctionnalisme en philosophie de l'esprit, soutient que le même type d'état mental peut être réalisé dans des substrats physiques différents, rendant la théorie de l'identité de type intenable et plaidant pour une caractérisation fonctionnelle.
hint: She maintained that the concept of multiple realisability, central to the philosophy of mind debate over functionalism, holds that the same mental state type can be realised in different physical substrates making type identity theory untenable and arguing for functional characterisation.
answers: She maintained that the concept of multiple realisability, central to the philosophy of mind debate over functionalism, holds that the same mental state type can be realised in different physical substrates making type identity theory untenable and arguing for functional characterisation.

en: Il a soutenu que la conscience phénoménale pose le défi le plus sérieux aux théories fonctionnalistes de l'esprit car le caractère qualitatif intrinsèque de l'expérience semble être laissé de côté par tout compte purement fonctionnel qui spécifie les états mentaux seulement en termes de leurs rôles causaux.
hint: He contended that phenomenal consciousness poses the most serious challenge to functionalist theories of mind because the intrinsic qualitative character of experience seems to be left out by any purely functional account that specifies mental states only in terms of their causal roles.
answers: He contended that phenomenal consciousness poses the most serious challenge to functionalist theories of mind because the intrinsic qualitative character of experience seems to be left out by any purely functional account that specifies mental states only in terms of their causal roles.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de fonctionnalisme en philosophie de l'esprit soutient que les états mentaux sont définis par leurs rôles fonctionnels leurs relations causales aux entrées sorties et autres états mentaux rendant leur réalisation physique non pertinente pour leur nature mentale.
hint: She argued that the concept of functionalism in the philosophy of mind holds that mental states are defined by their functional roles their causal relations to inputs outputs and other mental states making their physical realisation irrelevant to their mental nature.
answers: She argued that the concept of functionalism in the philosophy of mind holds that mental states are defined by their functional roles their causal relations to inputs outputs and other mental states making their physical realisation irrelevant to their mental nature.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'identité personnelle au cours du temps soulève des puzzles philosophiques fondamentaux sur ce qui fait qu'une personne à un moment est la même personne à un autre moment, Locke insistant sur la continuité psychologique, Parfit remettant en question l'importance de l'identité et les théories de la continuité physique.
hint: He maintained that the concept of personal identity over time raises fundamental philosophical puzzles about what makes a person at one time the same person at another time with Locke emphasising psychological continuity Parfit questioning the importance of identity and physical continuity theories.
answers: He maintained that the concept of personal identity over time raises fundamental philosophical puzzles about what makes a person at one time the same person at another time with Locke emphasising psychological continuity Parfit questioning the importance of identity and physical continuity theories.

en: Elle a soutenu que la vue réductionniste de Derek Parfit sur l'identité personnelle dans Reasons and Persons soutient que les personnes n'ont pas un statut de fait profond supplémentaire au-delà de la connexité et de la continuité psychologiques et que cela a de profondes implications pour la rationalité et l'éthique.
hint: She contended that Derek Parfit's reductionist view of personal identity in Reasons and Persons holds that persons do not have a deep further fact status over and above psychological connectedness and continuity and that this has profound implications for rationality and ethics.
answers: She contended that Derek Parfit's reductionist view of personal identity in Reasons and Persons holds that persons do not have a deep further fact status over and above psychological connectedness and continuity and that this has profound implications for rationality and ethics.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de chance morale, analysé par Nagel et Williams, révèle une tension profonde dans nos pratiques morales entre tenir les gens responsables de leurs actions et reconnaître que beaucoup de ce qui détermine les résultats échappe à leur contrôle.
hint: He argued that the concept of moral luck, analysed by Nagel and Williams, reveals a profound tension in our moral practices between holding people responsible for their actions and acknowledging that much of what determines outcomes is beyond their control.
answers: He argued that the concept of moral luck, analysed by Nagel and Williams, reveals a profound tension in our moral practices between holding people responsible for their actions and acknowledging that much of what determines outcomes is beyond their control.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'équilibre réfléchi dans la méthode de justification de Rawls soutient que la justification normative procède en cherchant la cohérence entre nos jugements particuliers réfléchis et les principes généraux en révisant chacun à la lumière de l'autre.
hint: She maintained that the concept of reflective equilibrium in Rawls's method of justification holds that normative justification proceeds by seeking coherence between our considered particular judgments and general principles revising each in light of the other.
answers: She maintained that the concept of reflective equilibrium in Rawls's method of justification holds that normative justification proceeds by seeking coherence between our considered particular judgments and general principles revising each in light of the other.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept du principe de différence dans la théorie de la justice de Rawls soutient que les inégalités sociales et économiques ne sont justifiées que si elles bénéficient aux membres les moins avantagés de la société, la justice exigeant une attention systématique à la position des plus défavorisés.
hint: He contended that the concept of the difference principle in Rawls's theory of justice holds that social and economic inequalities are only justified if they benefit the least advantaged members of society making justice require systematic attention to the position of the worst-off.
answers: He contended that the concept of the difference principle in Rawls's theory of justice holds that social and economic inequalities are only justified if they benefit the least advantaged members of society making justice require systematic attention to the position of the worst-off.

en: Elle a soutenu que la théorie des droits de Robert Nozick en matière de justice dans Anarchy, State and Utopia soutient que les distributions sont justes si elles résultent d'échanges libres à partir d'une acquisition originale juste et que tout principe de distribution à pattern nécessite une violation continue des droits individuels.
hint: She argued that Robert Nozick's entitlement theory of justice in Anarchy State and Utopia holds that distributions are just if they arise through free exchange from a just original acquisition and that any patterned principle of distribution requires continuous violation of individual rights.
answers: She argued that Robert Nozick's entitlement theory of justice in Anarchy State and Utopia holds that distributions are just if they arise through free exchange from a just original acquisition and that any patterned principle of distribution requires continuous violation of individual rights.

en: Il a soutenu que le débat philosophique entre le libertarisme et l'égalitarisme sur la justice distributive révèle une tension fondamentale entre le respect des droits et libertés individuels de propriété et l'assurance que chacun dispose de ressources suffisantes pour une autonomie véritable et une égalité des chances.
hint: He maintained that the philosophical debate between libertarianism and egalitarianism over distributive justice reveals a fundamental tension between respecting individual property rights and freedoms and ensuring that everyone has sufficient resources for genuine autonomy and equality of opportunity.
answers: He maintained that the philosophical debate between libertarianism and egalitarianism over distributive justice reveals a fundamental tension between respecting individual property rights and freedoms and ensuring that everyone has sufficient resources for genuine autonomy and equality of opportunity.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de suffisantarisme en justice distributive soutient que ce qui importe le plus moralement n'est pas l'égalité en soi mais s'assurer que tout le monde a assez, en priorité l'élimination de la privation sur la réduction de l'inégalité parmi les non-privés.
hint: She contended that the concept of sufficientarianism in distributive justice holds that what matters most morally is not equality per se but ensuring that everyone has enough prioritising the elimination of deprivation over reducing inequality among the non-deprived.
answers: She contended that the concept of sufficientarianism in distributive justice holds that what matters most morally is not equality per se but ensuring that everyone has enough prioritising the elimination of deprivation over reducing inequality among the non-deprived.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'égalitarisme de la chance, associé à Cohen, Dworkin et Arneson, soutient que la justice requiert de neutraliser les effets de la malchance brute sur les perspectives de vie des individus tout en permettant les conséquences de la malchance optionnelle résultant de choix volontaires.
hint: He argued that the concept of luck egalitarianism associated with Cohen Dworkin and Arneson holds that justice requires neutralising the effects of bad brute luck on individuals' life prospects while allowing consequences of option luck resulting from voluntary choices.
answers: He argued that the concept of luck egalitarianism associated with Cohen Dworkin and Arneson holds that justice requires neutralising the effects of bad brute luck on individuals' life prospects while allowing consequences of option luck resulting from voluntary choices.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept philosophique de contrat social dans sa lecture contemporaine est mieux compris comme un dispositif pour modéliser les conditions d'une autorité politique justifiée plutôt que comme un compte historique des origines de la société politique.
hint: She maintained that the philosophical concept of social contract in its contemporary reading is best understood as a device for modelling the conditions of justified political authority rather than as a historical account of the origins of political society.
answers: She maintained that the philosophical concept of social contract in its contemporary reading is best understood as a device for modelling the conditions of justified political authority rather than as a historical account of the origins of political society.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie analytique du langage fait face au défi du problème de Frege-Geach pour les théories expressivistes du discours moral qui montre que les phrases morales enchâssées dans des composés logiques ne peuvent être comprises comme de simples expressions d'attitude puisque leur comportement logique requiert un contenu propositionnel.
hint: He contended that the analytic philosophy of language faces the challenge of the Frege-Geach problem for expressivist theories of moral discourse which shows that moral sentences embedded in logical compounds cannot be understood as mere expressions of attitude since their logical behaviour requires propositional content.
answers: He contended that the analytic philosophy of language faces the challenge of the Frege-Geach problem for expressivist theories of moral discourse which shows that moral sentences embedded in logical compounds cannot be understood as mere expressions of attitude since their logical behaviour requires propositional content.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de concepts éthiques épais dans l'éthique de Bernard Williams décrit des concepts comme cruel courageux et juste qui sont simultanément descriptifs et évaluatifs et que la distinction entre fait et valeur est problématique pour comprendre le langage éthique.
hint: She argued that the concept of thick ethical concepts in Bernard Williams's ethics describes concepts like cruel brave and just that are simultaneously descriptive and evaluative and that the distinction between fact and value is problematic for understanding ethical language.
answers: She argued that the concept of thick ethical concepts in Bernard Williams's ethics describes concepts like cruel brave and just that are simultaneously descriptive and evaluative and that the distinction between fact and value is problematic for understanding ethical language.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de particularisme moral, associé à Jonathan Dancy, soutient que la pertinence morale de toute caractéristique d'une situation peut changer selon le contexte et qu'aucun principe moral n'a d'application invariante rendant l'éthique fondamentalement au cas par cas.
hint: He maintained that the concept of moral particularism, associated with Jonathan Dancy, holds that the moral relevance of any feature of a situation can change depending on context and that no moral principle has invariant application making ethics fundamentally case-by-case.
answers: He maintained that the concept of moral particularism, associated with Jonathan Dancy, holds that the moral relevance of any feature of a situation can change depending on context and that no moral principle has invariant application making ethics fundamentally case-by-case.

en: Elle a soutenu que le débat contemporain sur les intuitions morales en théorie éthique soulève des questions sur le statut épistémique des jugements moraux pré-théoriques certains les voyant comme des données fiables et d'autres comme de simples produits de la contingence évolutionnaire des biais et du conditionnement culturel.
hint: She contended that the contemporary debate over moral intuitions in ethical theory raises questions about the epistemic status of pre-theoretical moral judgments with some viewing them as reliable data points and others as mere products of evolutionary contingency biases and cultural conditioning.
answers: She contended that the contemporary debate over moral intuitions in ethical theory raises questions about the epistemic status of pre-theoretical moral judgments with some viewing them as reliable data points and others as mere products of evolutionary contingency biases and cultural conditioning.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de progrès moral soulève des questions philosophiques fondamentales sur ce que signifie le fait que la morale s'améliore si un standard moral objectif existe contre lequel le progrès peut être mesuré et comment rendre compte de l'expansion historique des cercles moraux.
hint: He argued that the concept of moral progress raises fundamental philosophical questions about what it means for morality to improve whether there is an objective moral standard against which progress can be measured and how to account for the historical expansion of moral circles.
answers: He argued that the concept of moral progress raises fundamental philosophical questions about what it means for morality to improve whether there is an objective moral standard against which progress can be measured and how to account for the historical expansion of moral circles.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'identité pratique dans l'éthique néo-kantienne de Christine Korsgaard soutient que ce que nous sommes obligés de faire est déterminé par les identités pratiques que nous endossons réflexivement créant des obligations normatives à travers la structure de l'auto-constitution réflexive.
hint: She maintained that the concept of practical identity in Christine Korsgaard's neo-Kantian ethics holds that what we are obligated to do is determined by the practical identities we reflectively endorse creating normative obligations through the structure of reflective self-constitution.
answers: She maintained that the concept of practical identity in Christine Korsgaard's neo-Kantian ethics holds that what we are obligated to do is determined by the practical identities we reflectively endorse creating normative obligations through the structure of reflective self-constitution.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'autonomie en philosophie morale et politique décrit la capacité des agents à se gouverner selon leurs propres principes et que respecter l'autonomie requiert de traiter les personnes comme des fins en elles-mêmes et non simplement comme des moyens générant des contraintes fondamentales sur le traitement permissible.
hint: He contended that the concept of autonomy in moral and political philosophy describes the capacity of agents to govern themselves according to their own principles and that respecting autonomy requires treating persons as ends in themselves and not merely as means generating foundational constraints on permissible treatment.
answers: He contended that the concept of autonomy in moral and political philosophy describes the capacity of agents to govern themselves according to their own principles and that respecting autonomy requires treating persons as ends in themselves and not merely as means generating foundational constraints on permissible treatment.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de dignité comme concept moral fondamental, développé dans l'éthique kantienne et adopté dans le droit international des droits humains, soutient que toutes les personnes ont une valeur inhérente qui ne peut être réduite à un prix de marché ou échangée contre des gains d'utilité.
hint: She argued that the concept of dignity as a foundational moral concept, developed in Kantian ethics and adopted in international human rights law, holds that all persons have an inherent worth that cannot be reduced to market price or exchanged for utility gains.
answers: She argued that the concept of dignity as a foundational moral concept, developed in Kantian ethics and adopted in international human rights law, holds that all persons have an inherent worth that cannot be reduced to market price or exchanged for utility gains.

en: Il a soutenu que le contractualisme en éthique tel qu'articulé par T.M. Scanlon soutient qu'une action est injuste si elle est régie par un principe que personne ne pourrait raisonnablement rejeter, fondant la moralité dans ce que nous nous devons mutuellement en tant que membres de la communauté morale.
hint: He maintained that contractualism in ethics as articulated by T.M. Scanlon holds that an action is wrong if it is governed by a principle that no one could reasonably reject grounding morality in what we owe to each other as members of the moral community.
answers: He maintained that contractualism in ethics as articulated by T.M. Scanlon holds that an action is wrong if it is governed by a principle that no one could reasonably reject grounding morality in what we owe to each other as members of the moral community.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de double effet en philosophie morale, associé à Aquinas et analysé par Foot et Thomson, soutient qu'il y a une différence moralement significative entre vouloir intentionnellement un dommage et le prévoir comme effet secondaire tout en poursuivant un bien.
hint: She contended that the concept of double effect in moral philosophy, associated with Aquinas and later analysed by Foot and Thomson, holds that there is a morally significant difference between intending harm and foreseeing it as a side effect when pursuing a good end.
answers: She contended that the concept of double effect in moral philosophy, associated with Aquinas and later analysed by Foot and Thomson, holds that there is a morally significant difference between intending harm and foreseeing it as a side effect when pursuing a good end.

en: Il a soutenu que l'expérience de pensée du problème du tramway, introduite par Foot et développée par Thomson, révèle une tension profonde entre le raisonnement conséquentialiste et déontologique nous forçant à confronter si la permissibilité du dommage dépend de la façon dont il est causé.
hint: He argued that the trolley problem thought experiment, introduced by Foot and developed by Thomson, reveals a deep tension in moral thinking between consequentialist and deontological reasoning forcing us to confront whether the permissibility of harm depends on how it is caused.
answers: He argued that the trolley problem thought experiment, introduced by Foot and developed by Thomson, reveals a deep tension in moral thinking between consequentialist and deontological reasoning forcing us to confront whether the permissibility of harm depends on how it is caused.

en: Elle a soutenu que l'éthique féministe défie la philosophie morale dominante pour son biais vers l'impartialité abstraite et plaide pour l'importance des relations particulières des responsabilités de soin de la vulnérabilité et de la nature incarnée et située des agents moraux.
hint: She maintained that feminist ethics challenges mainstream moral philosophy for its bias toward abstract impartiality and argues for the importance of particular relationships caring responsibilities vulnerability and the embodied situated nature of moral agents.
answers: She maintained that feminist ethics challenges mainstream moral philosophy for its bias toward abstract impartiality and argues for the importance of particular relationships caring responsibilities vulnerability and the embodied situated nature of moral agents.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie de la peine fait face à des questions fondamentales de justification entre les théories rétributives qui fondent la punition dans le mérite et les théories conséquentialistes qui la justifient par ses effets dissuasifs incapacitants ou réhabililitants sur la criminalité future.
hint: He contended that the philosophy of punishment faces fundamental questions about justification between retributive theories that ground punishment in desert and consequentialist theories that justify it by its deterrent incapacitative or rehabilitative effects on future crime.
answers: He contended that the philosophy of punishment faces fundamental questions about justification between retributive theories that ground punishment in desert and consequentialist theories that justify it by its deterrent incapacitative or rehabilitative effects on future crime.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de responsabilité en philosophie morale requiert de distinguer entre responsabilité causale, responsabilité morale, imputabilité et obligation de réparer, chacune avec des conditions différentes et des implications différentes pour le blâme, l'éloge et les obligations correctives.
hint: She argued that the concept of responsibility in moral philosophy requires distinguishing between causal responsibility moral responsibility accountability and liability each with different conditions and different implications for blame praise and remedial obligations.
answers: She argued that the concept of responsibility in moral philosophy requires distinguishing between causal responsibility moral responsibility accountability and liability each with different conditions and different implications for blame praise and remedial obligations.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de loi naturelle en philosophie politique et juridique soutient qu'il existe un ordre moral objectif découvrable par la raison auquel le droit positif doit se conformer et que les lois positives injustes manquent d'obligatoriété morale totale avec Aquinas, Locke et Finnis comme principaux partisans.
hint: He maintained that the concept of natural law in political and legal philosophy holds that there is an objective moral order discoverable by reason that positive law must conform to and that unjust positive laws lack full moral obligatoriness with Aquinas Locke and Finnis as major proponents.
answers: He maintained that the concept of natural law in political and legal philosophy holds that there is an objective moral order discoverable by reason that positive law must conform to and that unjust positive laws lack full moral obligatoriness with Aquinas Locke and Finnis as major proponents.

en: Elle a soutenu que le positivisme juridique en philosophie du droit, associé à Austin, Hart et Raz, soutient que l'existence et le contenu du droit dépendent de faits sociaux sur ce qui a été édicté et non de ses mérites, générant la célèbre thèse de la séparabilité entre droit et moralité.
hint: She contended that legal positivism in philosophy of law, associated with Austin Hart and Raz, holds that the existence and content of law depends on social facts about what has been enacted and not on its merits generating the famous separability thesis between law and morality.
answers: She contended that legal positivism in philosophy of law, associated with Austin Hart and Raz, holds that the existence and content of law depends on social facts about what has been enacted and not on its merits generating the famous separability thesis between law and morality.

en: Il a soutenu que l'interprétivisme de Ronald Dworkin en philosophie du droit soutient que le droit n'est pas simplement des règles édictées mais inclut les principes que la meilleure interprétation de la pratique juridique requiert et qu'il y a une bonne réponse aux cas juridiques difficiles générée par ces principes et valeurs.
hint: He argued that Ronald Dworkin's interpretivism in legal philosophy holds that law is not merely enacted rules but includes the principles that the best interpretation of legal practice requires and that there is one right answer to hard legal cases generated by these principles and values.
answers: He argued that Ronald Dworkin's interpretivism in legal philosophy holds that law is not merely enacted rules but includes the principles that the best interpretation of legal practice requires and that there is one right answer to hard legal cases generated by these principles and values.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept des études juridiques critiques, apparu dans les années 1970 et 1980, soutient que le droit n'est pas neutre ni apolitique mais reflète et reproduit les structures de pouvoir existantes et que la doctrine juridique est souvent indéterminée et ouverte à la contestation politique.
hint: She maintained that the concept of critical legal studies, emerging in the 1970s and 1980s, argues that law is not neutral or apolitical but reflects and reproduces existing power structures and that legal doctrine is often indeterminate and open to political contestation.
answers: She maintained that the concept of critical legal studies, emerging in the 1970s and 1980s, argues that law is not neutral or apolitical but reflects and reproduces existing power structures and that legal doctrine is often indeterminate and open to political contestation.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de pluralisme constitutionnel dans la théorie juridique européenne décrit la coexistence de plusieurs ordres constitutionnels au sein de l'Union européenne chacun faisant des revendications d'autorité ultime créant une nouvelle forme d'ordre juridique sans sommet hiérarchique unique.
hint: He contended that the concept of constitutional pluralism in European legal theory describes the coexistence of multiple constitutional orders within the European Union each making ultimate authority claims creating a new form of legal order without a single hierarchical summit.
answers: He contended that the concept of constitutional pluralism in European legal theory describes the coexistence of multiple constitutional orders within the European Union each making ultimate authority claims creating a new form of legal order without a single hierarchical summit.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de proportionnalité en droit constitutionnel et international est devenu une méthode dominante d'adjudication équilibrant les droits et intérêts concurrents, mais les critiques soutiennent qu'il donne aux tribunaux une discrétion excessive et substitue des jugements judiciaires à des jugements démocratiques.
hint: She argued that the concept of proportionality in constitutional and international law has become a dominant method of adjudication balancing competing rights and interests but critics argue it gives courts excessive discretion and substitutes judicial for democratic judgments.
answers: She argued that the concept of proportionality in constitutional and international law has become a dominant method of adjudication balancing competing rights and interests but critics argue it gives courts excessive discretion and substitutes judicial for democratic judgments.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de crise de légitimité décrit des situations où les institutions politiques existantes perdent leur prétention à l'autorité aux yeux des citoyens créant des conditions pour soit un renouveau démocratique un changement transformateur soit une réaction autoritaire.
hint: He maintained that the concept of legitimacy crisis describes situations where existing political institutions lose their claim to authority in the eyes of citizens creating conditions for either democratic renewal transformative change or authoritarian backlash.
answers: He maintained that the concept of legitimacy crisis describes situations where existing political institutions lose their claim to authority in the eyes of citizens creating conditions for either democratic renewal transformative change or authoritarian backlash.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de justice transitionnelle décrit l'ensemble des mécanismes judiciaires et non judiciaires que les sociétés utilisent lors de leur transition du régime autoritaire ou du conflit armé vers la paix et la démocratie pour faire face aux héritages des atrocités de masse et des violations des droits humains.
hint: She contended that the concept of transitional justice describes the set of judicial and non-judicial mechanisms societies use when transitioning from authoritarian rule or armed conflict to peace and democracy to address legacies of mass atrocity and human rights violations.
answers: She contended that the concept of transitional justice describes the set of judicial and non-judicial mechanisms societies use when transitioning from authoritarian rule or armed conflict to peace and democracy to address legacies of mass atrocity and human rights violations.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de politique de la mémoire décrit comment les acteurs politiques et les communautés se disputent l'interprétation des événements historiques particulièrement traumatiques et que les narratives historiques officielles sont toujours des expressions des relations de pouvoir présentes et des aspirations futures.
hint: He argued that the concept of memory politics describes how political actors and communities contest the interpretation of historical events particularly traumatic ones and that official historical narratives are always expressions of present power relations and future aspirations.
answers: He argued that the concept of memory politics describes how political actors and communities contest the interpretation of historical events particularly traumatic ones and that official historical narratives are always expressions of present power relations and future aspirations.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de commissions vérité et réconciliation, modélisées sur l'expérience sud-africaine, reflète une philosophie distincte de justice transitionnelle mettant l'accent sur la justice restauratrice plutôt que rétributive et sur la nécessité d'une reconnaissance publique des violations passées.
hint: She maintained that the concept of truth and reconciliation commissions, modelled on the South African experience, reflects a distinctive philosophy of transitional justice emphasising restorative over retributive justice and the need for public acknowledgment of past violations.
answers: She maintained that the concept of truth and reconciliation commissions, modelled on the South African experience, reflects a distinctive philosophy of transitional justice emphasising restorative over retributive justice and the need for public acknowledgment of past violations.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie de l'histoire débat si l'explication historique devrait suivre le même modèle nomologique-déductif que la science naturelle ou si elle requiert des approches compréhensives et interprétatives qui saisissent le sens des actions depuis les perspectives des agents.
hint: He contended that the philosophy of history debates whether historical explanation should follow the same deductive-nomological model as natural science or whether it requires understanding interpretive approaches that grasp the meaning of actions from the agents' perspectives.
answers: He contended that the philosophy of history debates whether historical explanation should follow the same deductive-nomological model as natural science or whether it requires understanding interpretive approaches that grasp the meaning of actions from the agents' perspectives.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'identité narrative, développé par Paul Ricoeur, soutient que les identités personnelles et collectives sont constituées par les histoires que nous racontons sur nous-mêmes et que comprendre l'expérience historique et personnelle requiert une configuration narrative de l'expérience temporelle.
hint: She argued that the concept of narrative identity, developed by Paul Ricoeur, holds that personal and collective identities are constituted through the stories we tell about ourselves and that understanding historical and personal experience requires narrative configuration of temporal experience.
answers: She argued that the concept of narrative identity, developed by Paul Ricoeur, holds that personal and collective identities are constituted through the stories we tell about ourselves and that understanding historical and personal experience requires narrative configuration of temporal experience.

en: Il a soutenu que l'herméneutique philosophique de Gadamer, développant le concept heideggérien de pré-structure, soutient que toute compréhension implique une fusion d'horizons entre l'interprète et le texte et que la tradition dans laquelle nous nous tenons favorise plutôt qu'elle n'entrave la compréhension.
hint: He maintained that Gadamer's philosophical hermeneutics, expanding on Heidegger's concept of fore-structure, argues that all understanding involves a fusion of horizons between the interpreter and the text and that the tradition within which we stand enables rather than hinders understanding.
answers: He maintained that Gadamer's philosophical hermeneutics, expanding on Heidegger's concept of fore-structure, argues that all understanding involves a fusion of horizons between the interpreter and the text and that the tradition within which we stand enables rather than hinders understanding.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de verstehen ou compréhension interprétative dans les sciences humaines, théorisé par Dilthey et Weber, soutient que l'explication scientifique sociale requiert de saisir les significations subjectives que les agents attribuent à leurs actions plutôt que de les subsumer sous des lois causales.
hint: She contended that the concept of verstehen or interpretive understanding in the human sciences, theorised by Dilthey and Weber, holds that social scientific explanation requires grasping the subjective meanings agents attribute to their actions rather than subsuming them under causal laws.
answers: She contended that the concept of verstehen or interpretive understanding in the human sciences, theorised by Dilthey and Weber, holds that social scientific explanation requires grasping the subjective meanings agents attribute to their actions rather than subsuming them under causal laws.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept des types idéaux de Max Weber décrit des construits théoriques qui mettent l'accent sur certaines caractéristiques de la réalité sociale à des fins analytiques sans prétendre représenter parfaitement la réalité historique servant de standards pour mesurer les déviations dans les cas empiriques.
hint: He argued that Max Weber's concept of ideal types describes theoretical constructs that emphasise certain features of social reality for analytical purposes without claiming to perfectly represent historical reality serving as standards for measuring deviations in empirical cases.
answers: He argued that Max Weber's concept of ideal types describes theoretical constructs that emphasise certain features of social reality for analytical purposes without claiming to perfectly represent historical reality serving as standards for measuring deviations in empirical cases.

en: Elle a soutenu que la thèse de l'éthique protestante de Weber soutient que l'esprit du capitalisme a trouvé une affinité élective avec l'éthique protestante calviniste notamment la doctrine de la prédestination générant un ascétisme intramondain qui a favorisé l'accumulation rationnelle systématique de la richesse.
hint: She maintained that Weber's Protestant Ethic thesis argues that the spirit of capitalism found an elective affinity with Calvinist Protestant ethics particularly the doctrine of predestination generating a this-worldly asceticism that fostered the systematic rational accumulation of wealth.
answers: She maintained that Weber's Protestant Ethic thesis argues that the spirit of capitalism found an elective affinity with Calvinist Protestant ethics particularly the doctrine of predestination generating a this-worldly asceticism that fostered the systematic rational accumulation of wealth.
