en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'émergence remet en question la réduction soutenant que certains phénomènes aux niveaux supérieurs d'organisation ont des propriétés qui ne sont pas présentes dans et ne peuvent pas être prédites des seuls constituants de niveau inférieur nécessitant de nouveaux principes explicatifs à chaque niveau.
hint: He contended that the concept of emergence challenges reduction holding that some phenomena at higher levels of organisation have properties that are not present in and cannot be predicted from the lower level constituents alone requiring new explanatory principles at each level.
answers: He contended that the concept of emergence challenges reduction holding that some phenomena at higher levels of organisation have properties that are not present in and cannot be predicted from the lower level constituents alone requiring new explanatory principles at each level.

en: Elle a soutenu que la philosophie des sciences sociales débat si les sciences sociales doivent viser à l'explication causale analogue à la science naturelle ou à la compréhension interprétative des significations sociales et si les résultats des sciences sociales peuvent avoir un pouvoir prédictif analogue à la science naturelle.
hint: She maintained that the philosophy of social science debates whether social science should aim at causal explanation analogous to natural science or interpretive understanding of social meanings and whether social scientific results can have predictive power analogous to natural science.
answers: She maintained that the philosophy of social science debates whether social science should aim at causal explanation analogous to natural science or interpretive understanding of social meanings and whether social scientific results can have predictive power analogous to natural science.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'individualisme méthodologique en sciences sociales soutient que les phénomènes sociaux doivent finalement être expliqués en termes d'actions de motivations et de croyances d'agents individuels et que les entités et structures macro-sociales n'ont pas de pouvoirs causaux indépendants.
hint: He argued that the concept of methodological individualism in social science holds that social phenomena must ultimately be explained in terms of the actions motivations and beliefs of individual agents and that macro-social entities and structures do not have independent causal powers.
answers: He argued that the concept of methodological individualism in social science holds that social phenomena must ultimately be explained in terms of the actions motivations and beliefs of individual agents and that macro-social entities and structures do not have independent causal powers.

en: Elle a soutenu que le collectivisme méthodologique ou holisme en sciences sociales soutient que les structures sociales ont des propriétés causales au-delà de celles des individus qui les composent et que les explications adéquates des phénomènes sociaux doivent se référer à ces structures sociales irréductibles.
hint: She contended that methodological collectivism or holism in social science holds that social structures have causal properties over and above those of the individuals who compose them and that adequate explanations of social phenomena must refer to these irreducible social structures.
answers: She contended that methodological collectivism or holism in social science holds that social structures have causal properties over and above those of the individuals who compose them and that adequate explanations of social phenomena must refer to these irreducible social structures.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'explication structurelle en sciences sociales soutient que les résultats sociaux sont mieux expliqués non pas par les intentions ou les choix des acteurs individuels mais par les structures objectives de positions sociales qui contraignent et habilitent certains modèles d'action.
hint: He maintained that the concept of structural explanation in social science holds that social outcomes are best explained not by the intentions or choices of individual actors but by the objective structures of social positions that constrain and enable certain patterns of action.
answers: He maintained that the concept of structural explanation in social science holds that social outcomes are best explained not by the intentions or choices of individual actors but by the objective structures of social positions that constrain and enable certain patterns of action.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de dépendance au sentier dans l'institutionnalisme historique décrit comment les premiers choix institutionnels contraignent les options futures en créant des mécanismes d'auto-renforcement qui rendent difficile le passage à des arrangements alternatifs même s'ils seraient plus efficaces.
hint: She argued that the concept of path dependency in historical institutionalism describes how early institutional choices constrain future options by creating self-reinforcing mechanisms that make it difficult to switch to alternative arrangements even when they would be more efficient.
answers: She argued that the concept of path dependency in historical institutionalism describes how early institutional choices constrain future options by creating self-reinforcing mechanisms that make it difficult to switch to alternative arrangements even when they would be more efficient.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de jonctions critiques dans l'institutionnalisme historique décrit des moments exceptionnels où les contraintes structurelles se relâchent et les alternatives institutionnelles deviennent disponibles, les choix faits aux jonctions critiques ayant des conséquences durables à travers la dépendance au sentier subséquente.
hint: He contended that the concept of critical junctures in historical institutionalism describes exceptional moments when structural constraints loosen and institutional alternatives become available with the choices made at critical junctures having long-lasting consequences through subsequent path dependence.
answers: He contended that the concept of critical junctures in historical institutionalism describes exceptional moments when structural constraints loosen and institutional alternatives become available with the choices made at critical junctures having long-lasting consequences through subsequent path dependence.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de gradualisme institutionnel en institutionnalisme historique décrit comment les institutions changent non seulement par des jonctions critiques mais par des processus incrémentiels de superposition de conversion de dérive et de déplacement qui s'accumulent dans le temps en une transformation significative.
hint: She maintained that the concept of gradualisme institutionnel in historical institutionalism describes how institutions change not only through critical junctures but through incremental processes of layering conversion drift and displacement that accumulate over time into significant transformation.
answers: She maintained that the concept of gradualisme institutionnel in historical institutionalism describes how institutions change not only through critical junctures but through incremental processes of layering conversion drift and displacement that accumulate over time into significant transformation.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de variétés de capitalisme, développé par Hall et Soskice, soutient que les économies de marché ne convergent pas vers un modèle unique mais existent sous des formes distinctes notamment les économies de marché libérales et les économies de marché coordonnées chacune avec des avantages institutionnels comparatifs différents.
hint: He argued that the concept of varieties of capitalism, developed by Hall and Soskice, holds that market economies are not converging on a single model but exist in distinct forms particularly liberal market economies and coordinated market economies each with different comparative institutional advantages.
answers: He argued that the concept of varieties of capitalism, developed by Hall and Soskice, holds that market economies are not converging on a single model but exist in distinct forms particularly liberal market economies and coordinated market economies each with different comparative institutional advantages.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de malédiction des ressources en économie politique décrit le paradoxe que les pays avec d'abondantes ressources naturelles ont souvent de moins bons résultats de développement économiques et politiques que les pays sans de telles ressources en raison de distorsions institutionnelles et de dynamiques autoritaires.
hint: She contended that the concept of the resource curse in political economy describes the paradox that countries with abundant natural resources often have worse developmental economic and political outcomes than countries without such resources due to institutional distortions and authoritarian dynamics.
answers: She contended that the concept of the resource curse in political economy describes the paradox that countries with abundant natural resources often have worse developmental economic and political outcomes than countries without such resources due to institutional distortions and authoritarian dynamics.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de mouvements sociaux en sociologie politique examine comment l'action collective contestataire remet en question les structures de pouvoir existantes, la théorie des nouveaux mouvements sociaux se concentrant sur l'identité les cadres culturels et les valeurs post-matérielles plutôt que sur les intérêts de classe.
hint: He maintained that the concept of social movements in political sociology examines how contentious collective action challenges existing power structures and institutional arrangements with new social movement theory focusing on identity cultural frames and post-material values rather than class interests.
answers: He maintained that the concept of social movements in political sociology examines how contentious collective action challenges existing power structures and institutional arrangements with new social movement theory focusing on identity cultural frames and post-material values rather than class interests.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de société civile en philosophie politique décrit la sphère des associations volontaires des institutions intermédiaires et des mouvements sociaux qui ne sont ni État ni marché et qui jouent des fonctions cruciales dans le maintien d'une culture politique démocratique et le contrôle du pouvoir étatique.
hint: She argued that the concept of civil society in political philosophy describes the sphere of voluntary associations intermediary institutions and social movements that are neither state nor market and that perform crucial functions in maintaining a democratic political culture and checking state power.
answers: She argued that the concept of civil society in political philosophy describes the sphere of voluntary associations intermediary institutions and social movements that are neither state nor market and that perform crucial functions in maintaining a democratic political culture and checking state power.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de sondage délibératif, développé par James Fishkin, décrit une forme de démocratie délibérative dans laquelle des citoyens sélectionnés aléatoirement délibèrent sur des questions politiques complexes transformant leurs opinions grâce à des informations équilibrées et une discussion structurée révélant des préférences réfléchies plutôt que spontanées.
hint: He contended that the concept of deliberative polling, developed by James Fishkin, describes a form of deliberative democracy in which randomly selected citizens deliberate about complex policy issues transforming their opinions through balanced information and structured discussion revealing considered rather than spontaneous preferences.
answers: He contended that the concept of deliberative polling, developed by James Fishkin, describes a form of deliberative democracy in which randomly selected citizens deliberate about complex policy issues transforming their opinions through balanced information and structured discussion revealing considered rather than spontaneous preferences.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de démocratie épistémique soutient que les procédures démocratiques sont précieuses non seulement parce qu'elles respectent l'autonomie individuelle mais aussi parce que l'agrégation de perspectives et de savoirs divers à travers des processus démocratiques peut conduire à de meilleures décisions que celles prises par des élites épistémiques.
hint: She maintained that the concept of epistemic democracy holds that democratic procedures are not valuable only because they respect individual autonomy but also because aggregating diverse perspectives and knowledge through democratic processes can lead to better decisions than those made by epistemic elites.
answers: She maintained that the concept of epistemic democracy holds that democratic procedures are not valuable only because they respect individual autonomy but also because aggregating diverse perspectives and knowledge through democratic processes can lead to better decisions than those made by epistemic elites.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de populisme en philosophie politique décrit une idéologie mince qui divise la société en un peuple pur et une élite corrompue et soutient que la politique devrait être l'expression de la volonté générale du peuple contre cette élite avec des variantes de gauche et de droite.
hint: He argued that the concept of populism in political philosophy describes a thin ideology that divides society into a pure people and a corrupt elite and claims that politics should be the expression of the general will of the people against this elite with both left and right variants.
answers: He argued that the concept of populism in political philosophy describes a thin ideology that divides society into a pure people and a corrupt elite and claims that politics should be the expression of the general will of the people against this elite with both left and right variants.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept de technocratie soulève des préoccupations démocratiques sur la délégation des décisions politiques à des experts techniques pouvant être isolés de la responsabilité démocratique et dont l'expertise technique ne confère pas automatiquement d'autorité sur des choix politiques chargés de valeurs.
hint: She contended that the concept of technocracy raises democratic concerns about the delegation of political decisions to technical experts who may be insulated from democratic accountability and whose technical expertise does not automatically confer authority on value-laden policy choices.
answers: She contended that the concept of technocracy raises democratic concerns about the delegation of political decisions to technical experts who may be insulated from democratic accountability and whose technical expertise does not automatically confer authority on value-laden policy choices.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie de l'immigration examine si les États ont le droit d'exclure les immigrants potentiels et si les frontières sont moralement justifiées, les partisans des frontières ouvertes soutenant que la liberté de circulation est un droit humain fondamental.
hint: He maintained that the philosophy of immigration examines whether states have the right to exclude would-be immigrants and whether borders are morally justified with open borders advocates arguing that freedom of movement is a fundamental human right.
answers: He maintained that the philosophy of immigration examines whether states have the right to exclude would-be immigrants and whether borders are morally justified with open borders advocates arguing that freedom of movement is a fundamental human right.

en: Elle a soutenu que la philosophie du langage développe la distinction entre contenu sémantique la signification littérale des phrases et contenu pragmatique ce que les locuteurs communiquent en contexte, l'implicature conversationnelle gricéenne rendant compte de l'écart entre ce qui est dit et ce qui est voulu.
hint: She argued that the philosophy of language develops the distinction between semantic content the literal meaning of sentences and pragmatic content what speakers communicate in context with Gricean conversational implicature accounting for the gap between what is said and what is meant.
answers: She argued that the philosophy of language develops the distinction between semantic content the literal meaning of sentences and pragmatic content what speakers communicate in context with Gricean conversational implicature accounting for the gap between what is said and what is meant.

en: Il a soutenu que la théorie des actes de langage développée par Austin et Searle soutient que le langage n'est pas seulement utilisé pour décrire la réalité mais pour effectuer des actions sociales à travers des actes illocutoires tels que promettre ordonner et s'excuser qui changent le statut normatif des participants.
hint: He contended that the theory of speech acts developed by Austin and Searle holds that language is not merely used to describe reality but to perform social actions through illocutionary acts such as promising ordering and apologising that change the normative status of participants.
answers: He contended that the theory of speech acts developed by Austin and Searle holds that language is not merely used to describe reality but to perform social actions through illocutionary acts such as promising ordering and apologising that change the normative status of participants.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept philosophique de normativité décrit la caractéristique distinctive des affirmations normatives qui prétendent guider l'action ou évaluer des états de choses et soulève la question de la relation entre faits normatifs et faits naturels et si les premiers peuvent être naturalisés.
hint: She maintained that the philosophical concept of normativity describes the distinctive feature of normative claims that they purport to guide action or evaluate states of affairs and raises the question of how normative facts relate to natural facts and whether they can be naturalized.
answers: She maintained that the philosophical concept of normativity describes the distinctive feature of normative claims that they purport to guide action or evaluate states of affairs and raises the question of how normative facts relate to natural facts and whether they can be naturalized.

en: Il a soutenu que la distinction entre l'ordre de la justification et l'ordre de la découverte en épistémologie et philosophie des sciences soutient que les processus psychologiques par lesquels les croyances ou théories se forment sont distincts des relations logiques et évidentielles qui les justifient.
hint: He argued that the distinction between the order of justification and the order of discovery in epistemology and philosophy of science holds that the psychological processes by which beliefs or theories are formed are distinct from the logical and evidential relations that justify them.
answers: He argued that the distinction between the order of justification and the order of discovery in epistemology and philosophy of science holds that the psychological processes by which beliefs or theories are formed are distinct from the logical and evidential relations that justify them.

en: Elle a soutenu que le fondationnalisme en épistémologie soutient que les croyances justifiées forment une structure où certaines croyances basiques sont fondationnelles étant justifiées sans inférence à partir d'autres croyances tandis que toutes les autres croyances justifiées tirent finalement leur justification de ces fondements.
hint: She contended that foundationalism in epistemology holds that justified beliefs form a structure where some basic beliefs are foundational being justified without inference from other beliefs while all other justified beliefs ultimately derive their justification from these foundations.
answers: She contended that foundationalism in epistemology holds that justified beliefs form a structure where some basic beliefs are foundational being justified without inference from other beliefs while all other justified beliefs ultimately derive their justification from these foundations.

en: Il a soutenu que le cohérentisme en épistémologie soutient que les croyances sont justifiées par leur appartenance à un système cohérent de croyances se soutenant mutuellement plutôt que par dérivation de croyances basiques soulevant des questions sur la définition de la cohérence et si la cohérence suit la vérité.
hint: He maintained that coherentism in epistemology holds that beliefs are justified by their membership in a coherent system of mutually supporting beliefs rather than by derivation from basic beliefs raising questions about how coherence is to be defined and whether coherence tracks truth.
answers: He maintained that coherentism in epistemology holds that beliefs are justified by their membership in a coherent system of mutually supporting beliefs rather than by derivation from basic beliefs raising questions about how coherence is to be defined and whether coherence tracks truth.

en: Elle a soutenu que le fiabilisme en épistémologie soutient qu'une croyance est justifiée si elle est produite par un processus cognitif fiable qui tend à produire des croyances vraies et que l'exigence internaliste que la justification soit accessible à la réflexion du croyant est erronée.
hint: She argued that reliabilism in epistemology holds that a belief is justified if it is produced by a reliable cognitive process one that tends to produce true beliefs and that the internalist requirement that justification be accessible to the believer's reflection is mistaken.
answers: She argued that reliabilism in epistemology holds that a belief is justified if it is produced by a reliable cognitive process one that tends to produce true beliefs and that the internalist requirement that justification be accessible to the believer's reflection is mistaken.

en: Il a soutenu que le problème du scepticisme en épistémologie, soulevé par le démon de Descartes et le cerveau dans une cuve de Putnam, remet en question nos prétentions ordinaires à la connaissance en soutenant que nous ne pouvons pas exclure les hypothèses sceptiques radicales montrant que nos preuves sont compatibles avec des mondes radicalement différents.
hint: He contended that the problem of scepticism in epistemology, raised by Descartes's demon and Putnam's brain in a vat, challenges our ordinary knowledge claims by arguing that we cannot rule out radical sceptical hypotheses showing that our evidence is compatible with radically different worlds.
answers: He contended that the problem of scepticism in epistemology, raised by Descartes's demon and Putnam's brain in a vat, challenges our ordinary knowledge claims by arguing that we cannot rule out radical sceptical hypotheses showing that our evidence is compatible with radically different worlds.

en: Elle a soutenu que le contextualisme en épistémologie soutient que les conditions de vérité des attributions de connaissance varient avec le contexte conversationnel de sorte que si un énoncé de la forme S sait que p est vrai dépend des standards opératifs dans le contexte d'attribution.
hint: She maintained that contextualism in epistemology holds that the truth conditions of knowledge attributions vary with the conversational context so that whether a statement of the form S knows that p is true depends on the standards operative in the context of attribution.
answers: She maintained that contextualism in epistemology holds that the truth conditions of knowledge attributions vary with the conversational context so that whether a statement of the form S knows that p is true depends on the standards operative in the context of attribution.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de savoir comment versus savoir que, débattu par Ryle et plus tard Gilbert et Stanley, concerne la question de savoir si la connaissance pratique de faire les choses est une forme distincte de connaissance de la connaissance propositionnelle ou si elle se réduit à la connaissance propositionnelle.
hint: He argued that the concept of knowledge how versus knowledge that, debated by Ryle and later Gilbert and Stanley, concerns whether practical knowledge how to do things is a distinct form of knowledge from propositional knowledge or whether it reduces to propositional knowledge.
answers: He argued that the concept of knowledge how versus knowledge that, debated by Ryle and later Gilbert and Stanley, concerns whether practical knowledge how to do things is a distinct form of knowledge from propositional knowledge or whether it reduces to propositional knowledge.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'esprit étendu, proposé par Clark et Chalmers, soutient que les processus cognitifs peuvent s'étendre au-delà des limites de la peau et du crâne dans l'environnement de sorte que les carnets les smartphones et d'autres ressources externes peuvent devenir partie de nos systèmes cognitifs.
hint: She contended that the concept of extended mind, proposed by Clark and Chalmers, holds that cognitive processes can extend beyond the boundary of the skin and skull into the environment so that notebooks smartphones and other external resources can become part of our cognitive systems.
answers: She contended that the concept of extended mind, proposed by Clark and Chalmers, holds that cognitive processes can extend beyond the boundary of the skin and skull into the environment so that notebooks smartphones and other external resources can become part of our cognitive systems.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de cognition distribuée, développé par Hutchins, soutient que les processus cognitifs sont distribués à travers les individus les groupes sociaux et les artefacts et que pour comprendre la cognition nous devons étudier l'ensemble du système cognitif plutôt que seulement le cerveau individuel.
hint: He maintained that the concept of distributed cognition, developed by Hutchins, holds that cognitive processes are distributed across individuals social groups and artefacts and that to understand cognition we must study the whole cognitive system rather than just the individual brain.
answers: He maintained that the concept of distributed cognition, developed by Hutchins, holds that cognitive processes are distributed across individuals social groups and artefacts and that to understand cognition we must study the whole cognitive system rather than just the individual brain.

en: Elle a soutenu que la philosophie de la créativité examine ce qui rend quelque chose créatif et les conditions qui permettent la pensée créatrice soulevant des questions sur la conscience l'intention la nouveauté l'utilité et dans quelle mesure les systèmes algorithmiques peuvent être véritablement créatifs.
hint: She argued that the philosophy of creativity examines what makes something creative and what conditions enable creative thought raising questions about whether creativity requires consciousness intention novelty usefulness and the extent to which algorithmic systems can be genuinely creative.
answers: She argued that the philosophy of creativity examines what makes something creative and what conditions enable creative thought raising questions about whether creativity requires consciousness intention novelty usefulness and the extent to which algorithmic systems can be genuinely creative.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie de l'agentivité examine ce qui distingue la véritable agentivité du simple mécanisme et soutient que les véritables agents ont la capacité d'évaluer et d'agir sur des raisons de façon que les simples mécanismes ne peuvent pas faire rendant l'agentivité une catégorie philosophiquement irréductible.
hint: He contended that the philosophy of agency examines what distinguishes genuine agency from mere mechanism and argues that genuine agents have the capacity to evaluate and act on reasons in ways that mere mechanisms cannot making agency a philosophically irreducible category.
answers: He contended that the philosophy of agency examines what distinguishes genuine agency from mere mechanism and argues that genuine agents have the capacity to evaluate and act on reasons in ways that mere mechanisms cannot making agency a philosophically irreducible category.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'agentivité morale soulève des questions sur les capacités que les organismes doivent avoir pour être des agents moraux à part entière capables d'être tenus responsables de leurs actions, la rationalité la sensibilité la réactivité aux raisons et l'auto-gouvernance étant des critères candidats.
hint: She maintained that the concept of moral agency raises questions about what capacities organisms must have to be full moral agents capable of being held responsible for their actions with rationality sentience responsiveness to reasons and self-governance being candidate criteria.
answers: She maintained that the concept of moral agency raises questions about what capacities organisms must have to be full moral agents capable of being held responsible for their actions with rationality sentience responsiveness to reasons and self-governance being candidate criteria.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie de la mort examine ce qu'est la mort si elle est mauvaise pour celui qui meurt la vue épicurienne la niant et dans quelle mesure nous devons craindre la mort soulevant des questions sur la valeur de l'existence continue et l'identité personnelle au cours du temps.
hint: He argued that the philosophy of death examines what death is whether it is bad for the one who dies the Epicurean view denying this and the extent to which we should fear death raising questions about the value of continued existence and personal identity over time.
answers: He argued that the philosophy of death examines what death is whether it is bad for the one who dies the Epicurean view denying this and the extent to which we should fear death raising questions about the value of continued existence and personal identity over time.

en: Elle a soutenu que l'argument épicurien que la mort n'est pas mauvaise pour celui qui meurt parce que quand la mort est nous ne sommes pas et quand nous sommes la mort n'est pas a été contesté par la vue de la privation associée à Nagel et Feldman soutenant que la mort est mauvaise parce qu'elle prive la personne de biens futurs.
hint: She contended that the Epicurean argument that death is not bad for the one who dies because when death is we are not and when we are death is not has been challenged by the deprivationist view associated with Nagel and Feldman holding that death is bad because it deprives the person of future goods.
answers: She contended that the Epicurean argument that death is not bad for the one who dies because when death is we are not and when we are death is not has been challenged by the deprivationist view associated with Nagel and Feldman holding that death is bad because it deprives the person of future goods.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'immortalité soulève des questions philosophiques sur la question de savoir si la vie éternelle serait désirable et si l'identité personnelle pourrait être maintenue sur une période infinie, Bernard Williams soutenant que l'immortalité serait soit ennuyeuse soit pas vraiment continue avec le moi présent.
hint: He maintained that the concept of immortality raises philosophical questions about whether eternal life would be desirable and whether personal identity could be maintained over an infinite period with Bernard Williams arguing that immortality would be either boring or not truly continuous with the present self.
answers: He maintained that the concept of immortality raises philosophical questions about whether eternal life would be desirable and whether personal identity could be maintained over an infinite period with Bernard Williams arguing that immortality would be either boring or not truly continuous with the present self.

en: Elle a soutenu que la philosophie du suicide soulève des questions morales sur la question de savoir si les individus ont le droit de mettre fin à leur propre vie, les arguments kantiens niant ce droit par devoir les arguments utilitaristes le permettant dans certains cas et les arguments basés sur l'autonomie le défendant.
hint: She argued that the philosophy of suicide raises moral questions about whether individuals have the right to end their own lives with Kantian arguments denying this right on grounds of duty utilitarian arguments permitting suicide in some cases and autonomy-based arguments defending this right.
answers: She argued that the philosophy of suicide raises moral questions about whether individuals have the right to end their own lives with Kantian arguments denying this right on grounds of duty utilitarian arguments permitting suicide in some cases and autonomy-based arguments defending this right.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de sens de la vie soulève la distinction entre le sens dans la vie qui concerne le sentiment subjectif que sa vie importe et vaut la peine et le sens de la vie qui demande une finalité ou une signification plus large que la vie a d'un point de vue cosmique ou objectif.
hint: He contended that the concept of meaning of life raises the distinction between meaning in life which concerns the subjective sense that one's life matters and is worthwhile and the meaning of life which asks for a larger purpose or significance that life has from some cosmic or objective standpoint.
answers: He contended that the concept of meaning of life raises the distinction between meaning in life which concerns the subjective sense that one's life matters and is worthwhile and the meaning of life which asks for a larger purpose or significance that life has from some cosmic or objective standpoint.

en: Elle a soutenu que les vues existentialistes sur le sens de la vie de Sartre et Camus à Beauvoir soutiennent que la vie n'a pas de sens inhérent mais que les individus créent du sens à travers leurs choix leurs engagements leurs projets et leurs investissements résistant à la condition absurde de l'existence humaine.
hint: She maintained that existentialist views on the meaning of life, from Sartre and Camus to Beauvoir, hold that life has no inherent meaning but that individuals create meaning through their choices commitments projects and engagements resisting the absurd condition of human existence.
answers: She maintained that existentialist views on the meaning of life, from Sartre and Camus to Beauvoir, hold that life has no inherent meaning but that individuals create meaning through their choices commitments projects and engagements resisting the absurd condition of human existence.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept d'absurde dans la philosophie de Camus décrit la confrontation entre le besoin de sens de l'humanité et le silence de l'univers et que la réponse appropriée n'est ni le suicide ni l'échappatoire religieux mais la révolte embrassant pleinement la vie malgré son absurdité fondamentale.
hint: He argued that the concept of the absurd in Camus's philosophy describes the confrontation between humanity's need for meaning and the universe's silence and that the appropriate response is not suicide nor religious escape but revolt embracing life fully despite its fundamental meaninglessness.
answers: He argued that the concept of the absurd in Camus's philosophy describes the confrontation between humanity's need for meaning and the universe's silence and that the appropriate response is not suicide nor religious escape but revolt embracing life fully despite its fundamental meaninglessness.

en: Elle a soutenu que la philosophie de l'espoir examine si l'espoir est une simple émotion une attitude épistémique nécessitant une probabilité raisonnable ou une disposition à agir malgré l'incertitude et soulève des questions sur le rôle que l'espoir joue dans le maintien de l'action humaine et de la vie morale.
hint: She contended that the philosophy of hope examines whether hope is a mere emotion an epistemic attitude requiring reasonable probability or a disposition to act despite uncertainty and raises questions about what role hope plays in sustaining human action and moral life.
answers: She contended that the philosophy of hope examines whether hope is a mere emotion an epistemic attitude requiring reasonable probability or a disposition to act despite uncertainty and raises questions about what role hope plays in sustaining human action and moral life.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie du bonheur examine la relation entre plaisir satisfaction des désirs biens objectifs et épanouissement, débattant si le bonheur est mieux compris hédonistiquement comme maximisation du plaisir ou en termes d'eudaimonia aristotélicienne comme bien vivre et bien agir.
hint: He maintained that the philosophy of happiness examines the relationship between pleasure desire satisfaction objective goods and flourishing debating whether happiness is best understood hedonistically as maximising pleasure or in terms of Aristotelian eudaimonia as living and acting well.
answers: He maintained that the philosophy of happiness examines the relationship between pleasure desire satisfaction objective goods and flourishing debating whether happiness is best understood hedonistically as maximising pleasure or in terms of Aristotelian eudaimonia as living and acting well.

en: Elle a soutenu que l'approche par les capacités d'Amartya Sen au développement humain soutient que le bon critère pour évaluer le bien-être et la justice n'est pas les ressources ni l'utilité mais les libertés réelles les capacités que les personnes ont de vivre des vies qu'elles ont des raisons de valoriser.
hint: She argued that Amartya Sen's capability approach to human development holds that the appropriate metric for assessing wellbeing and justice is not resources or utility but the real freedoms capabilities people have to live lives they have reason to value.
answers: She argued that Amartya Sen's capability approach to human development holds that the appropriate metric for assessing wellbeing and justice is not resources or utility but the real freedoms capabilities people have to live lives they have reason to value.

en: Il a soutenu que l'approche des capacités de Martha Nussbaum fournit une liste de capacités humaines centrales que toute société décente devrait fournir à tous les citoyens, soutenant que ces capacités ne sont pas réductibles les unes aux autres et que leur importance est fondationnelle pour la justice politique.

en: Il a soutenu que la philosophie des neurosciences soulève des questions sur la question de savoir si les neurosciences peuvent réduire la psychologie établissant que les états mentaux sont identiques aux états cérébraux ou si l'explication psychologique est irréductiblement distincte de l'explication neurale requérant une analyse scientifique à plusieurs niveaux.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de cognition incarnée, s'appuyant sur Merleau-Ponty et Varela, Thompson et Rosch, soutient que les processus cognitifs sont fondamentalement façonnés par la nature et la situation du corps dans le monde plutôt que d'être une manipulation abstraite de symboles dans un cerveau divoricé de son corps.
hint: He contended that the concept of embodied cognition, drawing on Merleau-Ponty and Varela Thompson and Rosch, holds that cognitive processes are fundamentally shaped by the nature and situation of the body in the world rather than being abstract symbol manipulation in a brain divorced from its body.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'enactivisme, développé par Varela, Thompson et Rosch, soutient que la cognition n'est pas la représentation d'un monde pré-donné mais l'enactement d'un monde à travers l'engagement sensorimoteur d'un organisme avec son environnement transformant l'organisme et l'environnement.
hint: She maintained that the concept of enactivism, developed by Varela Thompson and Rosch, holds that cognition is not representation of a pre-given world but the enactment of a world through the sensorimotor engagement of an organism with its environment transforming both the organism and the environment.

en: Il a soutenu que le concept de cognition 4E, désignant la cognition incarnée enactivée inscrite et étendue, représente un cluster d'approches connexes qui rejettent la vue computationnelle classique de l'esprit comme manipulation interne de symboles et soutiennent que la cognition est liée au corps à l'environnement et à la culture.

en: Elle a soutenu que le concept d'incarnation radicale en sciences cognitives et philosophie soutient que la cognition s'étend non seulement au corps mais à l'environnement plus large à travers le couplage entre cerveau corps et monde de sorte que les systèmes cognitifs doivent être étudiés comme des systèmes cerveau-corps-environnement.
